articles.titleTr: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
articles.summaryTr: The Ritz hotel in Paris, which is still owned by the Al Fayed family, is one of the properties searched by police.
articles.articleText: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say - Published French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse. The Paris prosecutor's office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released. In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities. It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner. - Mohamed Al Fayed accused of multiple rapes by staff - Published19 September 2024 Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor's office said. It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into "allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape". The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed. The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family. The Villa Windsor in western Paris, another property involved in the search, was a holiday home for the Al Fayed family. It was previously the home of King Edward VIII, following his abdication, and his wife Wallis Simpson. The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims: "At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities. "In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators. "Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations. "The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office." A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation. Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024. One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence. Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers. A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed's brother, Salah Fayed, who died in 2010. Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations. Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate. In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims. "Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further." The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities. "We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said. "We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated." The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like. "Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over." articles.articleTextTr: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say - Published French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse. The Paris prosecutor's office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released. In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities. It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner. - Mohamed Al Fayed accused of multiple rapes by staff - Published19 September 2024 Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor's office said. It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into "allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape". The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed. The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family. The Villa Windsor in western Paris, another property involved in the search, was a holiday home for the Al Fayed family. It was previously the home of King Edward VIII, following his abdication, and his wife Wallis Simpson. The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims: "At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities. "In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators. "Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations. "The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office." A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation. Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024. One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence. Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers. A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed's brother, Salah Fayed, who died in 2010. Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations. Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate. In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims. "Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further." The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities. "We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said. "We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated." The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like. "Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over." The management of the Ritz Paris told AFP news agency that it "does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour" and that it was ready "to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities". If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support is available at BBC Action Line. - Published27 September 2024 - Published24 August

articles.articleText: “Hortlak Kızın Hikayesi” Kasım'da Farklı Sahnelerde Seyirciyle Buluşuyor Türkiye ve İngiltere ortak yapımı “Hortlak Kızın Hikayesi”, 19 Haziran’da Londra’daki Collective Theatre’da gerçekleşen ön gösteriminin ve 25 Haziran’da DasDas’ta gerçekleşen Türkiye prömiyerinin ardından yeni sezonuna başladı. Yazar Derem Çıray’ın kaleme aldığı, yönetmenliğini Işık Kaya’nın üstlendiği oyun, Cazu karakterine hayat veren Iraz Akçam’ın tek kişilik performansıyla sahneye taşınıyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle On yedi yaşındaki Cazu’nun ölümünün ardından başlayan sıra dışı yolculuğunu konu alan oyun, kuşaklar boyunca susturulan, dışlanan ve “öteki” ilan edilen kadınların hikâyelerini fantastik ve gotik bir anlatı üzerinden ele alıyor. Ölüm sebebini bilmediği için öteki dünyaya kabul edilmeyen Cazu, bir hortlak olarak yaşayanların arasına geri döner. Ölümünün ardındaki gerçeği ararken, bir yandan da kendisine anlatılan hikâyelerin izini sürer ve kendi hikâyesini yeniden yazmaya başlar. “Hortlak Kızın Hikayesi”, bastırılmış kadın seslerini oyuna özgü bestelenen şarkıların desteğiyle de sahneye taşıyarak seyirciyi karanlık, şiirsel ve düşündürücü bir yolculuğa davet ediyor. Tek kişilik performansıyla oyunun merkezinde yer alan Iraz Akçam’a, farklı karakterleri seslendiren sanatçıların kayıtları eşlik ediyor. Deneysel anlatım dili, fiziksel performans öğeleri, müzik ve kara mizahın iç içe geçtiği yapım, kendine özgü sahne diliyle güncel tiyatronun disiplinlerarası yaklaşımını bir araya getiriyor. 60 dakika ve tek perde olan “Hortlak Kızın Hikayesi”, 13 Kasım’da yeniden DasDas’ta sahnelenecek ve 15 Kasım’da ise ilk kez Beyoğlu’nda, istos Sahne Aznavur’da seyirciyle buluşacak.

articles.articleText: Bakan Gürlek'ten fon soruşturmaları çıkışı: "Hiç kimse hukukun üzerinde değil" - Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, fon soruşturmalarında çok sayıda şüphelinin tutuklandığını, mal varlıklarına tedbir uygulandığını ve banka hesaplarının bloke edildiğini açıkladı. - Gürlek, tasfiyesi tamamlanan fonlarda yatırımcılara ödemelerin yapıldığını, diğer fonlara ilişkin işlemlerin sürdüğünü bildirdi. Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada fon soruşturmaları kapsamında yürütülen çalışmalara ilişkin bilgi verdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Suç yapılanmalarının mali bağlantılarının ve para hareketlerinin titizlikle incelendiğini belirten Gürlek, soruşturmalar kapsamında çok sayıda şüphelinin tutuklandığını, mal varlıklarına tedbir konulduğunu ve banka hesaplarının bloke edildiğini ifade etti. Tasfiye edilen fonlarda ödemeler başladı Yatırımcıların haklarının korunmasına yönelik çalışmaların devam ettiğini vurgulayan Gürlek, tasfiyesi tamamlanan fonlarda hak sahiplerine ödemelerin yapıldığını açıkladı. Diğer fonlara ilişkin işlemlerin ise sürdüğünü bildirdi. Gönüllü iadelerin hukuki sorumluluğu ortadan kaldırmayacağını belirten Gürlek, iyi niyetli yatırımcıların haklarının korunması, mağduriyetlerin giderilmesi ve suçtan elde edilen kazançların ortaya çıkarılması için ilgili kurumlarla koordineli çalışıldığını kaydetti. "Hiç kimsenin ekonomik gücü hukukun üzerinde değildir" Soruşturmaların kararlılıkla sürdürüleceğini belirten Gürlek, sorumluların adalet önünde hesap vermesi için sürecin takipçisi olacaklarını vurguladı. Gürlek, açıklamasında, "Hiç kimsenin makamı, unvanı veya ekonomik gücü kendisine hukukun üzerinde bir konum sağlayamaz. Ucu nereye giderse gitsin, sorumluların adalet önünde hesap vermesi için sürecin takipçisi olacağız." ifadelerini kullandı. Fon soruşturmaları kapsamında suç yapılanmalarının mali bağlantılarını ve para hareketlerini titizlikle araştırıyoruz. Çok sayıda şüpheli tutuklanırken malvarlıklarına tedbir uygulanmış, banka hesaplarına bloke konulmuştur. Tasfiyesi tamamlanan fonlarda hak sahiplerine ödemeler yapılmış, diğer fonlara ilişkin çalışmalar sürdürülmektedir. Gönüllü iadelerin hukuki sorumluluğu ortadan kaldırmayacağını özellikle vurguluyoruz. İyi niyetli yatırımcılarımızın haklarını korumak, mağduriyetleri gidermek ve suçtan elde edilen kazançları ortaya çıkarmak için tüm ilgili kurumlarımızla koordinasyon içinde çalışıyoruz. Hiç kimsenin makamı, ünvanı veya ekonomik gücü kendisine hukukun üzerinde bir konum sağlayamaz. Ucu nereye giderse gitsin, sorumluların adalet önünde hesap vermesi için sürecin takipçisi olacağız. 📍 TBMM Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonu — Akın Gürlek (@abakingurlek) November 10, 2026

articles.title: Poland’s lower house backs sanctions bill covering crypto freezes
articles.summary: The bill is now before the Senate and would broaden the grounds for adding people and companies to Poland’s national sanctions list.
articles.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
articles.titleTr: Poland’s lower house backs sanctions bill covering crypto freezes
articles.summaryTr: The bill is now before the Senate and would broaden the grounds for adding people and companies to Poland’s national sanctions list.
articles.articleText: Poland’s lower house backs sanctions bill covering crypto freezes The bill is now before the Senate and would broaden the grounds for adding people and companies to Poland’s national sanctions list. Poland’s lower house passed a bill that would broaden the country’s sanctions framework and explicitly include crypto assets among the funds authorities can freeze when imposing sanctions. The Sejm approved the government-backed Act on Restrictive Measures on Friday by 240 votes to 202, with one abstention, and forwarded it to the Senate on Monday, according to official parliamentary records. The bill explicitly includes crypto assets, as defined under the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), among financial funds that authorities could freeze when imposing sanctions. Poland’s interior minister would oversee the national sanctions list, with sanctions-listing decisions taking effect the day after authorities publish a designation. Affected individuals and companies could challenge the decision in administrative court, but the bill allows enforcement before a court ruling. Poland already maintains a national sanctions list under a 2022 law aimed at countering support for Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The bill would expand the grounds for imposing national sanctions to include certain foreign interference and information manipulation that pose a serious threat to national security. The Senate has 30 days to approve, amend or reject the legislation. If it takes no action, Poland’s Constitution treats the bill as approved in the form passed by the Sejm, allowing it to proceed to the president for consideration. Related: US Treasury cuts off MEXC over alleged $16B in illicit transactions

articles.titleTr: Here’s what happened in crypto today
articles.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
articles.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, Coinbase and Kalshi have joined four other firms backing the CFTC in a lawsuit over whether US exchanges can list perpetual futures tied to individual stocks, cybersecurity firm CertiK urged exchanges to impose hard dollar limits on hot-wallet holdings following the $6.3 billion Binance hack, and blockchain analytics firm Elliptic reported that North Korean hackers used newly created memecoins to launder stolen funds. Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures Coinbase, Kalshi and four other companies asked a federal court Monday to accept a brief backing the United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a lawsuit over perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. According to a proposed amicus brief shared Monday by Coinbase legal representative Molly Abraham, the group also includes Kraken parent Payward, trading companies DRW Holdings and Jump Trading, and crypto investment company Paradigm Operations. The companies argue that stock perpetual futures fall under existing US futures laws. The filing comes days after a federal judge found that the CFTC likely “exceeded its statutory authority” in allowing single-stock perpetuals to trade as security futures. The case could determine whether US exchanges can offer retail traders contracts that track individual stocks without expiring. On Nov. 3, the CFTC announced that single-stock perpetual futures, or stock perps, could begin trading on US-regulated exchanges for the first time. The Capital Markets Alliance Association (CMAA), a newly formed trade and advocacy group representing traditional financial market participants and whose members include Cboe and Citadel Securities, sued the CFTC last week, challenging the CFTC’s authority to allow the contracts to trade. Crypto exchanges need dollar caps on hot wallets, CertiK says Crypto exchanges should impose hard dollar limits on their hot-wallet holdings rather than relying solely on cold-storage ratios to measure security, according to cybersecurity firm CertiK. The recommendation came as several crypto exchanges recently disclosed how much they held in cold wallets, seeking to reassure customers after the record Binance hack that targeted its hot wallets. Crypto exchange Gate reported that 88.26% of its total assets were in cold storage, while Coinbase said it keeps more than 99% of customer assets offline. “Cold storage is a useful measure of online exposure, but it is not a standalone security score,” CertiK’s research team told Cointelegraph. CertiK said crypto exchanges should consider setting hot-wallet caps for each asset and blockchain according to the strictest of three limits: a percentage of customer liabilities, estimated withdrawal needs and an absolute loss ceiling based on the exchange’s financial resources and recovery capabilities. “Flexibility should support operating liquidity, while hard dollar ceilings and circuit breakers limit potential loss,” they said. North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, routing roughly $430,000 through six newly launched tokens on the NEAR blockchain, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. The tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch. The hackers used one set of wallets to swap stolen NEAR tokens for the new memecoins, then used another set to sell those memecoins back into the pools for NEAR. The swaps let them move funds without direct wallet-to-wallet transfers, though the transactions remained traceable onchain. Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain.

articles.title: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss
articles.summary: Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027.

articles.titleTr: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss
articles.summaryTr: Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027.
articles.articleText: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027. Wall Street’s embrace of Bitcoin has created the “best buying opportunity ever,” according to investor Mark Moss. Moss co-founded the Bitcoin Opportunity Fund, where he is an advisory partner. In 2025, UK-listed Satsuma Technology appointed him chief Bitcoin strategist. Moss tells Cointelegraph on the latest episode of Trade Secrets that he first bought Bitcoin in 2015 at about $300, during a recovery from a $1,000 to $200 plunge. “It was so risky,” Moss recalls of buying back then. In contrast, today, “you have consensus from the US government and Wall Street.” “But most people still think it’s a scam,” he says. That skepticism opens buying opportunities as Bitcoin starts to cross what Moss calls the “chasm” between early adopters and mainstream investors. Banks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have made Bitcoin easier to buy and financial advisers could help persuade clients who have stayed away previously to consider investing. Related: Strategy shareholders approve daily dividends for four preferred stocks Moss calls bottom but Bitcoin keeps falling Bitcoin briefly climbed above $80,000 after the Democrats took control of the US Congress in the midterm elections, then gave back those gains as tech stocks sold off. By Friday, it fell to $74,762, its lowest level since August and remains in the doldrums at the time of writing. Despite the selloff, Moss points to the reaction to the $6.3 billion Binance hack as a sign that sellers were running out. “The price didn’t really drop,” he says. Bitcoin fell to $76,320 after the breach and slid to $74,762 on Friday, erasing its post-election gains. It fell further to about $73,500 late Sunday, its lowest level since August, after Nvidia’s board announced it would investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Bitcoin found another bottom after reports of Nvidia CEO’s scandal. Source: CoinMarketCap Flows into US spot Bitcoin ETFs swung sharply during election week. The funds took in about $75 million on Wednesday, then shed $430 million on Thursday. History is on the side of hodlers however. Bitcoin gained an average of about 53% in the 12 months after previous US midterms, Moss says, using data going back to 2014. That leaves three completed election cycles in his sample. He says he expects Bitcoin to set a new all-time high in 2027. Moss backs Strategy but would keep his Bitcoin Moss thinks the Bitcoin treasury company to own is Strategy (MSTR), but believes that holding Bitcoin yourself is still superior. Strategy began buying Bitcoin in 2020 and turned those purchases into a core part of its business. It has used stock and debt sales to fund its purchases, giving investors a way to bet on Bitcoin through a publicly traded company. By Nov. 2, Strategy held 849,327 BTC, more than 4% of Bitcoin’s maximum supply. “I don’t think there’s another publicly traded company that will outperform Strategy over the next ten years,” Moss says. Strategy has the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin trove. Source: BitcoinTreasuries.Net Leverage can help a Bitcoin treasury company’s shares outperform the cryptocurrency it holds when its price rises. But even if Strategy outperforms, Moss wouldn’t trade his Bitcoin holdings for its shares. Related: 1inch lawyer sees agencies driving US crypto regulation as midterms unfold Before Moss bought his first Bitcoin, he made a living buying foreclosed properties, fixing them up and selling them. He moved into property development, then built and sold a medical equipment business. He says he put the proceeds into Southern California real estate. When the market crashed in 2008, he lost it all. “The reward of being right is not worth the risk of getting it wrong,” he says. Even with his outlook for Strategy, Moss says he’d keep his Bitcoin and use only a small share of his portfolio to pursue higher returns through treasury stocks. A journey of $1 million Bitcoin starts with small allocations In Moss’s model, Bitcoin could reach $1 million under certain circumstances, when it competes with stocks, bonds, gold and real estate for a considerable share of investors’ wealth. The model estimates how much those assets are worth, projects how that pool could grow as the global money supply expands and calculates a Bitcoin price based on the share it captures. Financial advisers could help bring in that money via one client’s portfolio at a time, encouraging them to shift a few percentage points out of stocks or bonds and into Bitcoin. The scenario depends on a critical mass of clients doing that, to the point where all those small allocations add up. The model also assumes Bitcoin stays secure and decentralized. Asked what could derail the scenario, Moss pointed to a failure that compromised either feature. Moss says $1 million is possible by 2030... though hodler’s might have to wait until 2032. Hodler’s Digest: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms

articles.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
articles.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
articles.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
articles.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
articles.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
articles.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
articles.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

articles.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
articles.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

articles.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
articles.verification: Birincil kaynak
articles.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
articles.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

news.summaryTr: Slovyansk continues to be bombarded by Russian forces, making it almost uninhabitable with less than 10% of it's pre-war population remaining.
news.articleText: Meet the Peaky Blinders, Ukraine's drone unit protecting a devastated front-line city The BBC's Jonathan Beale reported from inside Slovyansk, one of four cities that make up Ukraine's "fortress belt" - a system of heavily reinforced defence lines in the parts of eastern region of Donetsk still under its control. The town has become almost uninhabitable and has been under heavy bombardment from Russian drones, missiles and glide bombs. Members of a Ukrainian drone unit that call themselves Peaky Blinders, named after the cult BBC TV series, have taken on the task of intercepting Russian drones. Russia wants Kyiv to give up the fortress cities and they are central to talks on a possible peace deal that have resumed after nine months between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi.

news.summary: ABD Enerji Enformasyon İdaresi (EIA), ülkede doğal gaz üretimi ve tüketiminin 2026 ve 2027 yıllarında yeni rekor seviyelere ulaşmasını bekliyor. Doğal gaz üretiminin 2027'de günlük 117,6 milyar fit küpe çıkacağı öngörülüyor.

news.titleTr: ABD'de doğal gaz üretimi ve tüketimi 2026 ve 2027'de rekor kıracak
news.summaryTr: ABD Enerji Enformasyon İdaresi (EIA), ülkede doğal gaz üretimi ve tüketiminin 2026 ve 2027 yıllarında yeni rekor seviyelere ulaşmasını bekliyor. Doğal gaz üretiminin 2027'de günlük 117,6 milyar fit küpe çıkacağı öngörülüyor.
news.articleText: ABD'de doğal gaz üretimi ve tüketimi 2026 ve 2027'de rekor kıracak - ABD Enerji Enformasyon İdaresi (EIA), ülkede doğal gaz üretimi ve tüketiminin 2026 ve 2027 yıllarında yeni rekor seviyelere ulaşmasını bekliyor. Doğal gaz üretiminin 2027'de günlük 117,6 milyar fit küpe çıkacağı öngörülüyor. ABD Enerji Enformasyon İdaresi (EIA), yayımladığı Kısa Vadeli Enerji Görünümü raporunda ülkenin doğal gaz üretimi ve tüketimine ilişkin tahminlerini açıkladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Buna göre ABD'nin kuru doğal gaz üretiminin 2025'te günlük 107,6 milyar fit küple kaydedilen rekor seviyeden 2026'da 113 milyar fit küpe, 2027'de ise 117,6 milyar fit küpe yükselmesi bekleniyor. Ülkedeki doğal gaz tüketiminin de artışını sürdürmesi öngörülüyor. Tüketimin 2025'te günlük 91,9 milyar fit küple ulaştığı rekor seviyeden 2026'da 92,3 milyar fit küpe, 2027'de 94,4 milyar fit küpe çıkacağı tahmin ediliyor. Tahminlerin gerçekleşmesi halinde 2026, doğal gaz talebinde üst üste beşinci rekor yıl olacak. LNG ihracatının 2027'de 19 milyar fit küpe çıkması bekleniyor EIA, ABD'nin sıvılaştırılmış doğal gaz (LNG) ihracatının da güçlü artış göstereceğini öngörüyor. Günlük ortalama LNG ihracatının 2025'teki 15,1 milyar fit küplük rekor seviyeden 2026'da 17,6 milyar fit küpe, 2027'de ise 19 milyar fit küpe yükselmesi bekleniyor. EIA'nın kasım ayı üretim tahmini, ekim ayında açıklanan 2026 öngörüsündeki günlük 112,2 milyar fit küp seviyesinin üzerine çıktı. Buna karşılık tüketim tahmini, önceki 92,4 milyar fit küplük beklentinin altında kaldı. Kömür üretiminde 1963'ten bu yana en düşük seviye bekleniyor Elektrik üreticilerinin önümüzdeki yıllarda daha az kömür kullanmasının beklendiğini belirten EIA, ABD'nin kömür üretiminde düşüş öngördü. Buna göre kömür üretiminin 2025'teki 528,4 milyon kısa ton seviyesinden 2026'da 518,5 milyon tona, 2027'de ise 495,4 milyon tona gerilemesi bekleniyor. Bu tahminin gerçekleşmesi halinde üretim 1963'ten bu yana en düşük seviyeye inecek. Fosil yakıt kaynaklı emisyonlar 2027'de yeniden artacak EIA, fosil yakıtlardan kaynaklanan karbondioksit emisyonlarının 2025'teki 4,916 milyar metrik ton seviyesinden 2026'da 4,844 milyar tona düşeceğini tahmin ediyor. Petrol ve kömür kullanımındaki azalışın etkisiyle beklenen bu düşüşün ardından, petrol ve doğal gaz tüketimindeki artışla emisyonların 2027'de 4,856 milyar tona yükselmesi öngörülüyor.

news.titleTr: Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions
news.summaryTr: Najib Razak was convicted for his role in the billion-dollar scandal involving the 1MDB sovereign wealth fund.
news.articleText: Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions - Published Malaysia's disgraced former Prime Minister Najib Razak has arrived home to begin serving the rest of a jail sentence for corruption under house arrest. There was a big media presence at his Kuala Lumpur residence to see the 73-year-old return from prison in an SUV late on Tuesday night, escorted by a heavily armed police convoy. Najib's return ended a four-year prison stint after he was found guilty over the embezzlement of billions of dollars from the country's sovereign wealth fund. The 1MDB scandal brought down his government and made headlines around the world when it came to light a decade ago, embroiling prominent figures from Malaysia to Goldman Sachs and Hollywood. Investigators estimated that $4.5bn (£3.3bn) was siphoned from the state-owned wealth fund, which Najib co-founded, into private pockets, including his own. More than $1bn allegedly ended up in accounts linked to Najib, according to prosecutors. Najib's lawyers claim he had been misled by his advisers - in particular the financier Jho Low, who has maintained his innocence and remains at large. Najib's mansion in one of the capital's most exclusive neighbourhoods was declared a federal prison ahead of his homecoming on Tuesday. Critics said his release from jail undermined efforts to fight corruption and questioned its legal basis, saying Malaysian law made no provision for house arrest. Najib, who was prime minister from 2009 to 2018, denied wrongdoing but was convicted at two separate trials. In the first trial he was sentenced in 2020 to 12 years in prison and jailed in 2022. The term was later halved on appeal. In September, the King of Malaysia granted him a conditional pardon to see out the remaining two years of his sentence at home. The transfer to his mansion was to take place on Friday but put on hold after the attorney general sought clarification of the royal decree. On Tuesday the high court ruled the house arrest was effective immediately. Najib's party paid a $12m fine as part of the terms of the royal pardon allowing him to serve the rest of his term at home. He was sentenced after being convicted of abuse of power, money laundering and breach of trust over 42 million ringgit ($10m; £7.7m) transferred from SRC International - a former unit of 1MDB - into his private accounts. news.summary: Starting next week, customers can deposit and withdraw money through Brazil’s instant payment system. Crypto transfers remain suspended.

news.titleTr: Mercado Bitcoin to resume cash withdrawals after $49M hack
news.summaryTr: Starting next week, customers can deposit and withdraw money through Brazil’s instant payment system. Crypto transfers remain suspended.
news.articleText: Mercado Bitcoin to resume cash withdrawals after $49M hack Starting next week, customers can deposit and withdraw money through Brazil’s instant payment system. Crypto transfers remain suspended. Crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin will resume deposits and withdrawals in Brazilian reais via Pix, the country’s instant payment system, next week, a company representative told Cointelegraph. The restart will come more than 15 days after an attack drained an estimated $49 million from wallets linked to the exchange. Customers will only be able to withdraw funds to accounts in their own name. Mercado Bitcoin will also credit customers’ accounts with proceeds from the settlement of fixed income products. Crypto deposits and withdrawals remain suspended, with no date set for their return. Mercado Bitcoin, one of Brazil’s largest crypto exchanges, began restoring access on Monday, a week after the attack, by allowing customers to view their accounts in read-only mode. Customers who regain access are directed to a page detailing the exchange’s security measures and regular audits since 2018, with a link to a separate account of the incident. Fabricio Tota, Mercado Bitcoin’s vice president of new business, outlined the next phase in a recent video. The exchange has yet to publish a rollout schedule on its website. “The resumption will proceed gradually, and the rollout of additional services will be communicated to clients in advance through MB’s official channels,” the representative said. The Nov. 2 attack on Mercado Bitcoin came four days after hackers stole about $6.3 billion in crypto from Binance’s hot wallets in a separate breach. The FBI attributed the Binance theft to North Korean hackers. The crypto exchange said it would cover the losses using its emergency fund and corporate treasury. news.title: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
news.summary: The ruling brings to an end an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
news.summaryTr: The ruling brings to an end an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones.
news.articleText: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned - Published A UK court has overturned laws criminalising same-sex intimacy in Trinidad and Tobago. London's Judicial Committee of the Privy Council (JCPC), the Caribbean island's final court of appeal, ruled the laws were not in keeping with the "fundamental individual right to respect for private and family life." The judgement is the result of an 11-year legal battle brought by dual-citizen Jason Jones, 62, who said he hoped it would "accelerate the fight for full equality." Jones had successfully challenged the laws in 2018 in Trinidad's High Court, however the ruling was overturned on appeal by the Trinidadian government. It is the first time the JCPC has ever decided on a case to decriminalise same-sex intimacy, and campaigners hope it will spark similar successful legal challenges elsewhere in the Commonwealth. Prior to this historic decision, Trinidad and Tobago was one of some 34 Commonwealth countries continuing to criminalise homosexuality based on colonial-era British laws. Under these laws, consensual same-sex intimacy is punishable by imprisonment, and in some cases carries the death penalty. The Attorney General of Trinidad and Tobago had argued that the law was protected from legal challenges by the "savings law clauses" - which carried over existing British laws into newly independent states. Representatives for Jones argued that the laws violated an individual's right to privacy and argued the government's changes to the laws in 1986 - which saw stricter punishments introduced - meant the savings clause protections no longer applied. The judicial committee unanimously found in favour of Jones. Handing down the judgement, Lord Sales told the court the laws "cannot be regarded as reasonably justifiable in a society that has a proper respect for the rights and freedoms of an individual". Jones, human rights campaigner and appellant in the appeal, said: "These laws never reflected who we are as a people and a nation - diverse, multiracial, and secular. "They told LGBTQ+ people that we were criminals in our own country. That message ends today." Lawyer Anand Ramlogan SC, representing Jones, said the judgement was a "landmark victory for gay rights, equal dignity and respect for private and family life in Trinidad and Tobago." news.title: US federal authorities could have prevented Epstein crimes, report finds
news.summary: The report by a Republican-led congressional committee follows a 15-month investigation into the handling of the late disgraced financier's case.

news.titleTr: US federal authorities could have prevented Epstein crimes, report finds
news.summaryTr: The report by a Republican-led congressional committee follows a 15-month investigation into the handling of the late disgraced financier's case.
news.articleText: US federal authorities could have prevented Epstein crimes, report finds - Published Crimes committed by the late disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein after 2005 could have been prevented were it not for "failures" by federal investigators and prosecutors, a congressional investigation has concluded. The Republican-led US House Oversight Committee on Tuesday released its final report into what it described as the "decades-long" mishandling of the criminal investigations into Epstein and his long-term associate Ghislaine Maxwell. The report's findings are based on interviews and depositions with witnesses, government files, and financial records over a 15-month period. Epstein died in 2019 as he awaited trial on sex trafficking charges. "While some of these failures involved an exercise in poor judgement by the USAO, others appeared to be the result of Epstein's pervasive and wide-reaching influence," the report reads, referring to the US Attorney's Office. It states that, rather than fully investigating allegations in other states, the USAO for the Southern District of Florida entered an agreement with Epstein in 2007 allowing him to evade federal prosecution. Regarding Epstein's death in a New York prison, investigators concluded this was a result of "a series of institutional failures at the facility," which included staffing shortages, overworked employees, poor recordkeeping, and lax security practices. Testimony the panel solicited was "unable to definitively dispel certain theories" surrounding Epstein's death, the report states, including accounting for a lapse in surveillance footage. It found the justice department (DoJ) failed to communicate about document releases and that deficient redactions exposed survivors' sensitive personal information. Earlier this year, the DoJ had to remove thousands of documents related to Epstein from its website after victims said their identities had been compromised. The report also alleges that financial institutions like American Express enabled human trafficking and immigration fraud, by allowing Epstein to use decoy flights and dummy itineraries to transport foreign workers across borders. The BBC has contacted American Express for comment. The investigative panel recommended that Congress should pass legislation to prevent the weaponisation of non-disclosure agreements, which they said Epstein used to silence survivors. "Epstein operated with impunity, shielded and enabled by powerful connections and a justice system that repeatedly failed his victims," said James Comer, the Republican chairman of the committee. He called upon the DoJ to "interview or re-interview key witnesses, investigate Epstein associates accused of criminal activity, and ensure survivors have access to their records. The report accuses Democrats of being "obsessed" with trying to implicate US President Donald Trump and that an "unfounded witch hunt continued without regard for the interests of survivors". Trump has previously said he was friendly with Epstein before they fell out in 2004. The president's name has appeared thousands of times in the Epstein files but there is no suggestion that appearing in the documents implies any wrongdoing. The committee's review of documents did not identify any that would implicate Trump, the report concluded. In a statement, Rep Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the Oversight Committee, alleged his Republican colleagues "released a report based on an incomplete investigation and zero public hearings on Jeffrey Epstein". Garcia accused the justice department of withholding "over 2.5 million pages of documents". "We will not allow the President and his allies to dismiss this investigation," said Garcia, who is expected to lead the committee when Democrats take control of Congress in January following the recent midterm elections. - Published23 April

news.title: Anthropic set for $1.3tn stock market debut despite 'catastrophic' AI warning
news.summary: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78, which is lower than what was expected.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Anthropic set for $1.3tn stock market debut despite 'catastrophic' AI warning
news.summaryTr: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78, which is lower than what was expected.
news.articleText: Anthropic set for $1.3tn stock market debut despite 'catastrophic' AI warning - Published Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) company behind the Claude chatbot, could be valued at around $1.3 trillion (£1 trillion) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange. The loss-making company says it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each and will raise up to $64bn when it floats this month. It would value Anthropic at between $1.1tn and $1.3tn which, although large, is below the $2tn some backers of the firm predicted in summer, according to the Financial Times. The huge valuation comes despite the company warning last month that AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity". It is floating at a volatile time for big tech firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres. There are also wider fears over the billions of dollars being spent on AI and whether it will pay off. In its most recent results for the six months to the end of June, Anthropic's revenues jumped to $16.2bn from $1.1bn in the same period last year. However, its pre-tax loss jumped to $80.7bn from $12.9bn. Fiona Cincotta, a senior market analyst at City Index, said the $64bn Anthropic wants to raise is "fairly bullish" within "the volatility [and] concerns towards AI that we've seen in sort of particularly last week". She told Reuters: "It's showing that they are still sort of upbeat about the outlook as far as AI is concerned and that obviously that they think that the demand is going to be there." Anthropic, which will list under the symbol ANT on 19 November, will be the first fully AI-focused company to go public, making it a test case for the future of the technology. At $1.3tn, Anthropic's possible valuation is below SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence company, which listed its shares in June and was valued at nearly $1.8tn. - Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe - Published4 days ago - Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know - Published26 October Anthropic is just five years old. It was co-founded in 2021 by brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei along with five others – all of whom worked at OpenAI, the rival AI giant behind ChatGPT. It announced its intention to list on the stock market in June and OpenAI followed suit. That listing is now expected to occur early next year. The listing announcements were followed by a series of incidents involving AI agents, which are bots designed to operate somewhat autonomously, going rogue. Current and former staff of both companies have warned AI technology was being developed without the ability to protect humanity from possible future harms enacted by AI. Anthropic has admitted that advanced AI systems "could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponised, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy". The company has reiterated promises to develop AI to be beneficial to people. It has warned investors its future success depends largely on its ability to develop the most advanced AI models, and that "any failure to do so could adversely affect our business".

news.articleText: Tüm hisseler devredildi: İki kamu bankası TVF çatısı altında buluştu - Türkiye Varlık Fonu, Ziraat Katılım ve Halk Katılım bankalarının tüm hisselerini TVF Katılım Finans Yatırımları AŞ'ye devretti. İşlemlerin tamamlanmasıyla iki kamu sermayeli katılım bankası aynı çatı altında toplandı. Türkiye Varlık Fonu (TVF), Ziraat Katılım ve Halk Katılım bankalarının paylarının tamamının TVF Katılım Finans Yatırımları AŞ'ye devredildiğini duyurdu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle TVF'nin internet sitesinden yapılan açıklamaya göre, 7 Ekim 2026 tarihinde duyurulan pay devir sözleşmeleri kapsamında ilgili yasal ve düzenleyici süreçler tamamlandı. Devir işlemlerinin kapanışı da gerçekleştirildi. Kamu sermayeli katılım bankaları tek çatı altında Devir işlemiyle kamu sermayeli katılım finans kurumlarının aynı çatı altında toplanmasına yönelik süreçte önemli bir aşama tamamlanmış oldu. Düzenlemeyle katılım finans kurumlarının kapasitesinin ve rekabet gücünün artırılması, finansal piyasalar içerisindeki paylarının büyütülmesi hedefleniyor. TVF'den katılım finans ekosistemi vurgusu Türkiye Varlık Fonu, yatırım stratejisi doğrultusunda finansal piyasaların derinleşmesine ve katılım finans ekosisteminin gelişmesine katkı sağlamaya yönelik çalışmalarını sürdüreceğini bildirdi.

news.title: Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December
news.summary: US inflation came in above forecasts in October, increasing expectations of a bigger rate hike in December and raising concerns for crypto investors.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December
news.summaryTr: US inflation came in above forecasts in October, increasing expectations of a bigger rate hike in December and raising concerns for crypto investors.
news.articleText: Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December US inflation came in above forecasts in October, increasing expectations of a bigger rate hike in December and raising concerns for crypto investors. Crypto industry experts warned on Tuesday that higher-than-expected US inflation could lead to a another Federal Reserve interest rate hike, making borrowing more expensive and potentially discouraging investment in cryptocurrencies. The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% month over month in October, above economists’ forecast of 0.3%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics - a slower increase than September’s 0.6% rise. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, above the expected 0.2%. Currently, the Federal Reserve holds its benchmark interest rate at 3.75% to 4.00%, after raising it by a quarter-point in September and leaving it unchanged in October. The report came just a few hours after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said in London that another core inflation reading of 0.3% or higher could prompt the Fed to consider a larger interest rate hike in December. “In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting,” Waller said. “Hiking only 25-basis-points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take.” Markets were already pricing a quarter-point Fed hike in December. Tuesday’s data and Waller’s remarks are now raising the odds that the Fed would tighten monetary policy more aggressively in December, potentially raising borrowing costs and squeezing returns for leveraged crypto investors. Related: US midterm elections 2026 as it happened: Democrats win control of Congress Crypto experts warn of higher borrowing costs After the CPI release, traders were pricing in slightly more than a quarter point of Fed tightening for December, according to Jeff Anderson, head of US at crypto trading firm STS Digital. “Following today’s CPI release, markets are now pricing approximately 27 basis points of tightening into the December rate curve,” Anderson said in comments shared with Cointelegraph. “The prospect of another rate hike is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.” CME FedWatch data as of 16:28 UTC on Tuesday showed an 88.3% chance of a quarter-point rate hike in December and an 11.7% chance of a half-point increase. Meanwhile, the broader crypto market was trading lower following the report, with total market capitalization falling 1.6% over the past 24 hours to $2.57 trillion, according to CoinGecko. Bitcoin (BTC) traded near $73,274, down 2% over the past 24 hours, while Ether (ETH) fell nearly 5% to around $2,028 and Solana (SOL) dropped 5.6% to $82. Experts said that higher interest rates could also reduce profits from some crypto investments. Adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, told Cointelegraph that investors who borrow money to make other investments could earn less if borrowing becomes more expensive. “Carry strategies earn the gap between what their assets yield and what they pay to borrow, so they are squeezed when borrowing costs rise relative to that yield,” Haeems said. “Over the past two weeks the rate paid to USDC lenders on Aave’s main market ranged from about 3.2% to 7%, while three-month Treasury yields stayed close to 4.2%.” The difference, in turn, could influence where investors put their money, especially if traditional investments offer better returns with less risk. Inflation adds to pressure after US midterms The inflation report also came a week after the US midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of both the House and Senate. “There is also likely to be growing political pressure from a blue Congress to bring inflation under control, potentially reinforcing the case for higher rates,” Anderson said. Still, he added that he remained skeptical about whether further rate hikes would address the underlying causes of inflation. While Congress does not set interest rates, lawmakers can influence economic policy and crypto regulation. For instance, the CLARITY Act, a bill aimed at creating clearer crypto rules for the US, has been stalled since January amid disagreements between Democrats and Republicans. The shift in congressional power combined with the possibility of higher borrowing costs could create even more uncertainty for crypto investors, experts said. news.title: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
news.summary: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
news.summaryTr: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
news.articleText: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says - Published The first of two days of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine has concluded in Abu Dhabi. While senior officials from Kyiv and Moscow were tight-lipped after the four hour-long discussions, President Volodymyr Zelensky, who was not at the talks, said they had proved "constructive and quite substantive". Speaking from Paris, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said the meeting had been "very productive". Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said earlier that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario. Zelensky also said that humanitarian issues such as prisoner of war exchanges had been discussed. At the start of Tuesday's talks President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, told delegates that the US had "narrowed the gaps" between the two sides, without providing details, and hoped to move towards a "solution that hopefully ends the war". Kushner had said earlier the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine. He and Trump peace envoy Steve Witkoff also met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials on the sidelines of the main meeting. Until now European leaders have largely been excluded from peace talks, but they have pushed to be included in the discussions amid concerns that decisions about their continent's security would be made without them. The Americans appear to support this, with Rubio acknowledging during a visit to Paris that the Europeans "are a part of solving this problem for the long term". However, "the Russians have a bad taste in their mouth with the Europeans", according to a US official. Some proposals favoured by EU officials - such as calling an unconditional ceasefire as a prerequisite for peace negotiations - are routinely rejected by Moscow. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Tuesday that a truce would just allow Kyiv to regroup. "We will not agree to it," he said. Moscow and Kyiv's positions are still far apart on ending the conflict. A key area of disagreement involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are crucial to its future security. While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately". However, he acknowledged the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture". "They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other." For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it comes under attack again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from Eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans. The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022. The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since. From the start of his second term in office, US President Donald Trump – who once boasted he could end the war in Ukraine within a day – has spearheaded several rounds of talks to end the conflict, albeit with little success. Meanwhile, his increasingly conciliatory approach towards Moscow has fuelled deep unease in Kyiv and across the European Union. After meeting Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington last week, Trump touted a forthcoming "big, beautiful agreement" on Ukraine that "might involve all of Europe". Many in Ukraine are sceptical that this would result in a fair peace. Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believed Trump wanted "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv. The only way to make Russia's Vladimir Putin start real negotiations was by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said. "While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war". Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi includes Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky. Kyiv has sent several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya. Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof that Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms. On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations". "This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism." news.summary: Yapı Kredi, uluslararası piyasalardan yaklaşık 933 milyon dolar tutarında sendikasyon kredisi sağladı. 18 ülkeden 40 finansal kurumun katıldığı anlaşma, 367 ve 734 gün vadeli dört ayrı dilimden oluştu.

news.titleTr: Yapı Kredi'den (YKBNK) 933 milyon dolarlık dev sendikasyon kredisi! İşte detaylar
news.summaryTr: Yapı Kredi, uluslararası piyasalardan yaklaşık 933 milyon dolar tutarında sendikasyon kredisi sağladı. 18 ülkeden 40 finansal kurumun katıldığı anlaşma, 367 ve 734 gün vadeli dört ayrı dilimden oluştu.
news.articleText: Yapı Kredi'den (YKBNK) 933 milyon dolarlık dev sendikasyon kredisi! İşte detaylar - Yapı Kredi, uluslararası piyasalardan yaklaşık 933 milyon dolar tutarında sendikasyon kredisi sağladı. 18 ülkeden 40 finansal kurumun katıldığı anlaşma, 367 ve 734 gün vadeli dört ayrı dilimden oluştu. Yapı ve Kredi Bankası, yılın ikinci yarısında uluslararası piyasalardan yaklaşık 933 milyon dolar tutarında sendikasyon kredisi sağladı. Bankadan yapılan açıklamaya göre anlaşmaya 18 ülkeden 40 finansal kurum katıldı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 367 ve 734 gün vadeli dört ayrı dilimden oluşan kredinin ortak koordinatörlüğünü Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank, Bank of America, Emirates NBD ve Standard Chartered üstlendi. İşlemin aracılığını ise Emirates NBD gerçekleştirdi. Kredinin detayları belli oldu Sendikasyon kredisi kapsamında 367 gün vadeli 349 milyon dolar ve 356,5 milyon avro, 734 gün vadeli ise 97 milyon dolar ve 77 milyon avro finansman sağlandı. Kredinin maliyeti vade ve para birimine göre farklılık gösterdi. Buna göre 367 gün vadeli dilimlerde dolar için SOFR + yüzde 1,25, avro için Euribor + yüzde 1,00 maliyet belirlendi. 734 gün vadeli dilimlerde ise dolar maliyeti SOFR + yüzde 1,75, avro maliyeti Euribor + yüzde 1,45 oldu. Erün: Türkiye ekonomisine duyulan güvenin göstergesi Yapı Kredi Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) Gökhan Erün, uluslararası piyasalardan sağlanan kaynağın bankanın finansal yapısına ve Türkiye ekonomisine duyulan güveni gösterdiğini belirtti. Erün, yaklaşık 933 milyon dolarlık işlemin uluslararası finans kuruluşlarıyla kurulan uzun soluklu ilişkilerin bir yansıması olduğunu ifade etti. Uluslararası kuruluşların ilgisinin arkasında bankanın sağlam bilanço yapısı, etkin risk yönetimi ve sürdürülebilir büyüme anlayışının bulunduğunu vurgulayan Erün, gelecek dönemde kaynak çeşitliliğini artırmaya ve reel sektörün finansman ihtiyaçlarını desteklemeye devam edeceklerini kaydetti.
