news.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-

items.summaryTr: Slovyansk continues to be bombarded by Russian forces, making it almost uninhabitable with less than 10% of it's pre-war population remaining.
items.articleText: Meet the Peaky Blinders, Ukraine's drone unit protecting a devastated front-line city The BBC's Jonathan Beale reported from inside Slovyansk, one of four cities that make up Ukraine's "fortress belt" - a system of heavily reinforced defence lines in the parts of eastern region of Donetsk still under its control. The town has become almost uninhabitable and has been under heavy bombardment from Russian drones, missiles and glide bombs. Members of a Ukrainian drone unit that call themselves Peaky Blinders, named after the cult BBC TV series, have taken on the task of intercepting Russian drones. Russia wants Kyiv to give up the fortress cities and they are central to talks on a possible peace deal that have resumed after nine months between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi.

items.titleTr: ABD'de doğal gaz üretimi ve tüketimi 2026 ve 2027'de rekor kıracak
items.summaryTr: ABD Enerji Enformasyon İdaresi (EIA), ülkede doğal gaz üretimi ve tüketiminin 2026 ve 2027 yıllarında yeni rekor seviyelere ulaşmasını bekliyor. Doğal gaz üretiminin 2027'de günlük 117,6 milyar fit küpe çıkacağı öngörülüyor.
items.articleText: ABD'de doğal gaz üretimi ve tüketimi 2026 ve 2027'de rekor kıracak - ABD Enerji Enformasyon İdaresi (EIA), ülkede doğal gaz üretimi ve tüketiminin 2026 ve 2027 yıllarında yeni rekor seviyelere ulaşmasını bekliyor. Doğal gaz üretiminin 2027'de günlük 117,6 milyar fit küpe çıkacağı öngörülüyor. ABD Enerji Enformasyon İdaresi (EIA), yayımladığı Kısa Vadeli Enerji Görünümü raporunda ülkenin doğal gaz üretimi ve tüketimine ilişkin tahminlerini açıkladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Buna göre ABD'nin kuru doğal gaz üretiminin 2025'te günlük 107,6 milyar fit küple kaydedilen rekor seviyeden 2026'da 113 milyar fit küpe, 2027'de ise 117,6 milyar fit küpe yükselmesi bekleniyor. Ülkedeki doğal gaz tüketiminin de artışını sürdürmesi öngörülüyor. Tüketimin 2025'te günlük 91,9 milyar fit küple ulaştığı rekor seviyeden 2026'da 92,3 milyar fit küpe, 2027'de 94,4 milyar fit küpe çıkacağı tahmin ediliyor. Tahminlerin gerçekleşmesi halinde 2026, doğal gaz talebinde üst üste beşinci rekor yıl olacak. LNG ihracatının 2027'de 19 milyar fit küpe çıkması bekleniyor EIA, ABD'nin sıvılaştırılmış doğal gaz (LNG) ihracatının da güçlü artış göstereceğini öngörüyor. Günlük ortalama LNG ihracatının 2025'teki 15,1 milyar fit küplük rekor seviyeden 2026'da 17,6 milyar fit küpe, 2027'de ise 19 milyar fit küpe yükselmesi bekleniyor. EIA'nın kasım ayı üretim tahmini, ekim ayında açıklanan 2026 öngörüsündeki günlük 112,2 milyar fit küp seviyesinin üzerine çıktı. Buna karşılık tüketim tahmini, önceki 92,4 milyar fit küplük beklentinin altında kaldı. Kömür üretiminde 1963'ten bu yana en düşük seviye bekleniyor Elektrik üreticilerinin önümüzdeki yıllarda daha az kömür kullanmasının beklendiğini belirten EIA, ABD'nin kömür üretiminde düşüş öngördü. Buna göre kömür üretiminin 2025'teki 528,4 milyon kısa ton seviyesinden 2026'da 518,5 milyon tona, 2027'de ise 495,4 milyon tona gerilemesi bekleniyor. Bu tahminin gerçekleşmesi halinde üretim 1963'ten bu yana en düşük seviyeye inecek. Fosil yakıt kaynaklı emisyonlar 2027'de yeniden artacak EIA, fosil yakıtlardan kaynaklanan karbondioksit emisyonlarının 2025'teki 4,916 milyar metrik ton seviyesinden 2026'da 4,844 milyar tona düşeceğini tahmin ediyor. Petrol ve kömür kullanımındaki azalışın etkisiyle beklenen bu düşüşün ardından, petrol ve doğal gaz tüketimindeki artışla emisyonların 2027'de 4,856 milyar tona yükselmesi öngörülüyor.

items.titleTr: Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions
items.summaryTr: Najib Razak was convicted for his role in the billion-dollar scandal involving the 1MDB sovereign wealth fund.
items.articleText: Malaysia's disgraced former PM leaves jail for house arrest after embezzling millions - Published Malaysia's disgraced former Prime Minister Najib Razak has arrived home to begin serving the rest of a jail sentence for corruption under house arrest. There was a big media presence at his Kuala Lumpur residence to see the 73-year-old return from prison in an SUV late on Tuesday night, escorted by a heavily armed police convoy. Najib's return ended a four-year prison stint after he was found guilty over the embezzlement of billions of dollars from the country's sovereign wealth fund. The 1MDB scandal brought down his government and made headlines around the world when it came to light a decade ago, embroiling prominent figures from Malaysia to Goldman Sachs and Hollywood. Investigators estimated that $4.5bn (£3.3bn) was siphoned from the state-owned wealth fund, which Najib co-founded, into private pockets, including his own. More than $1bn allegedly ended up in accounts linked to Najib, according to prosecutors. Najib's lawyers claim he had been misled by his advisers - in particular the financier Jho Low, who has maintained his innocence and remains at large. Najib's mansion in one of the capital's most exclusive neighbourhoods was declared a federal prison ahead of his homecoming on Tuesday. Critics said his release from jail undermined efforts to fight corruption and questioned its legal basis, saying Malaysian law made no provision for house arrest. Najib, who was prime minister from 2009 to 2018, denied wrongdoing but was convicted at two separate trials. In the first trial he was sentenced in 2020 to 12 years in prison and jailed in 2022. The term was later halved on appeal. In September, the King of Malaysia granted him a conditional pardon to see out the remaining two years of his sentence at home. The transfer to his mansion was to take place on Friday but put on hold after the attorney general sought clarification of the royal decree. On Tuesday the high court ruled the house arrest was effective immediately. Najib's party paid a $12m fine as part of the terms of the royal pardon allowing him to serve the rest of his term at home. He was sentenced after being convicted of abuse of power, money laundering and breach of trust over 42 million ringgit ($10m; £7.7m) transferred from SRC International - a former unit of 1MDB - into his private accounts. Najib is appealing against a 15-year prison sentence, handed down at a second trial in December 2025, in a case involving much larger sums of money. In that case he was convicted of misappropriating nearly 2.3 billion Malaysian ringgit ($569m; £422m) from the nation's sovereign wealth fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB). He is due to start serving that sentence after his house arrest ends, which is expected in August 2028. Related topics - Published28 July 2020 - Published9 August 2019 - Published3 July 2018

items.summary: Starting next week, customers can deposit and withdraw money through Brazil’s instant payment system. Crypto transfers remain suspended.

items.titleTr: Mercado Bitcoin to resume cash withdrawals after $49M hack
items.summaryTr: Starting next week, customers can deposit and withdraw money through Brazil’s instant payment system. Crypto transfers remain suspended.
items.articleText: Mercado Bitcoin to resume cash withdrawals after $49M hack Starting next week, customers can deposit and withdraw money through Brazil’s instant payment system. Crypto transfers remain suspended. Crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin will resume deposits and withdrawals in Brazilian reais via Pix, the country’s instant payment system, next week, a company representative told Cointelegraph. The restart will come more than 15 days after an attack drained an estimated $49 million from wallets linked to the exchange. Customers will only be able to withdraw funds to accounts in their own name. Mercado Bitcoin will also credit customers’ accounts with proceeds from the settlement of fixed income products. Crypto deposits and withdrawals remain suspended, with no date set for their return. Mercado Bitcoin, one of Brazil’s largest crypto exchanges, began restoring access on Monday, a week after the attack, by allowing customers to view their accounts in read-only mode. Customers who regain access are directed to a page detailing the exchange’s security measures and regular audits since 2018, with a link to a separate account of the incident. Fabricio Tota, Mercado Bitcoin’s vice president of new business, outlined the next phase in a recent video. The exchange has yet to publish a rollout schedule on its website. “The resumption will proceed gradually, and the rollout of additional services will be communicated to clients in advance through MB’s official channels,” the representative said. The Nov. 2 attack on Mercado Bitcoin came four days after hackers stole about $6.3 billion in crypto from Binance’s hot wallets in a separate breach. The FBI attributed the Binance theft to North Korean hackers. The crypto exchange said it would cover the losses using its emergency fund and corporate treasury. Magazine: Asian crypto exchanges batten down the hatches as hacks surge: Asia Express

items.title: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
items.summary: The ruling brings to an end an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned
items.summaryTr: The ruling brings to an end an 11-year legal battle by dual-citizen Jason Jones.
items.articleText: Anti-homosexuality laws in Trinidad and Tobago overturned - Published A UK court has overturned laws criminalising same-sex intimacy in Trinidad and Tobago. London's Judicial Committee of the Privy Council (JCPC), the Caribbean island's final court of appeal, ruled the laws were not in keeping with the "fundamental individual right to respect for private and family life." The judgement is the result of an 11-year legal battle brought by dual-citizen Jason Jones, 62, who said he hoped it would "accelerate the fight for full equality." Jones had successfully challenged the laws in 2018 in Trinidad's High Court, however the ruling was overturned on appeal by the Trinidadian government. It is the first time the JCPC has ever decided on a case to decriminalise same-sex intimacy, and campaigners hope it will spark similar successful legal challenges elsewhere in the Commonwealth. Prior to this historic decision, Trinidad and Tobago was one of some 34 Commonwealth countries continuing to criminalise homosexuality based on colonial-era British laws. Under these laws, consensual same-sex intimacy is punishable by imprisonment, and in some cases carries the death penalty. The Attorney General of Trinidad and Tobago had argued that the law was protected from legal challenges by the "savings law clauses" - which carried over existing British laws into newly independent states. Representatives for Jones argued that the laws violated an individual's right to privacy and argued the government's changes to the laws in 1986 - which saw stricter punishments introduced - meant the savings clause protections no longer applied. The judicial committee unanimously found in favour of Jones. Handing down the judgement, Lord Sales told the court the laws "cannot be regarded as reasonably justifiable in a society that has a proper respect for the rights and freedoms of an individual". Jones, human rights campaigner and appellant in the appeal, said: "These laws never reflected who we are as a people and a nation - diverse, multiracial, and secular. "They told LGBTQ+ people that we were criminals in our own country. That message ends today." Lawyer Anand Ramlogan SC, representing Jones, said the judgement was a "landmark victory for gay rights, equal dignity and respect for private and family life in Trinidad and Tobago." items.articleText: US federal authorities could have prevented Epstein crimes, report finds - Published Crimes committed by the late disgraced financier Jeffrey Epstein after 2005 could have been prevented were it not for "failures" by federal investigators and prosecutors, a congressional investigation has concluded. The Republican-led US House Oversight Committee on Tuesday released its final report into what it described as the "decades-long" mishandling of the criminal investigations into Epstein and his long-term associate Ghislaine Maxwell. The report's findings are based on interviews and depositions with witnesses, government files, and financial records over a 15-month period. Epstein died in 2019 as he awaited trial on sex trafficking charges. "While some of these failures involved an exercise in poor judgement by the USAO, others appeared to be the result of Epstein's pervasive and wide-reaching influence," the report reads, referring to the US Attorney's Office. It states that, rather than fully investigating allegations in other states, the USAO for the Southern District of Florida entered an agreement with Epstein in 2007 allowing him to evade federal prosecution. Regarding Epstein's death in a New York prison, investigators concluded this was a result of "a series of institutional failures at the facility," which included staffing shortages, overworked employees, poor recordkeeping, and lax security practices. Testimony the panel solicited was "unable to definitively dispel certain theories" surrounding Epstein's death, the report states, including accounting for a lapse in surveillance footage. It found the justice department (DoJ) failed to communicate about document releases and that deficient redactions exposed survivors' sensitive personal information. Earlier this year, the DoJ had to remove thousands of documents related to Epstein from its website after victims said their identities had been compromised. The report also alleges that financial institutions like American Express enabled human trafficking and immigration fraud, by allowing Epstein to use decoy flights and dummy itineraries to transport foreign workers across borders. The BBC has contacted American Express for comment. The investigative panel recommended that Congress should pass legislation to prevent the weaponisation of non-disclosure agreements, which they said Epstein used to silence survivors. "Epstein operated with impunity, shielded and enabled by powerful connections and a justice system that repeatedly failed his victims," said James Comer, the Republican chairman of the committee. He called upon the DoJ to "interview or re-interview key witnesses, investigate Epstein associates accused of criminal activity, and ensure survivors have access to their records. The report accuses Democrats of being "obsessed" with trying to implicate US President Donald Trump and that an "unfounded witch hunt continued without regard for the interests of survivors". Trump has previously said he was friendly with Epstein before they fell out in 2004. The president's name has appeared thousands of times in the Epstein files but there is no suggestion that appearing in the documents implies any wrongdoing. The committee's review of documents did not identify any that would implicate Trump, the report concluded. In a statement, Rep Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the Oversight Committee, alleged his Republican colleagues "released a report based on an incomplete investigation and zero public hearings on Jeffrey Epstein". Garcia accused the justice department of withholding "over 2.5 million pages of documents". "We will not allow the President and his allies to dismiss this investigation," said Garcia, who is expected to lead the committee when Democrats take control of Congress in January following the recent midterm elections. - Published23 April

items.summaryTr: The AI company behind the Claude chatbot will offer its shares at between $70 and $78, which is lower than what was expected.
items.articleText: Anthropic set for $1.3tn stock market debut despite 'catastrophic' AI warning - Published Anthropic, the artificial intelligence (AI) company behind the Claude chatbot, could be valued at around $1.3 trillion (£1 trillion) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange. The loss-making company says it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each and will raise up to $64bn when it floats this month. It would value Anthropic at between $1.1tn and $1.3tn which, although large, is below the $2tn some backers of the firm predicted in summer, according to the Financial Times. The huge valuation comes despite the company warning last month that AI could pose "catastrophic or existential risks to humanity". It is floating at a volatile time for big tech firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres. There are also wider fears over the billions of dollars being spent on AI and whether it will pay off. In its most recent results for the six months to the end of June, Anthropic's revenues jumped to $16.2bn from $1.1bn in the same period last year. However, its pre-tax loss jumped to $80.7bn from $12.9bn. Fiona Cincotta, a senior market analyst at City Index, said the $64bn Anthropic wants to raise is "fairly bullish" within "the volatility [and] concerns towards AI that we've seen in sort of particularly last week". She told Reuters: "It's showing that they are still sort of upbeat about the outlook as far as AI is concerned and that obviously that they think that the demand is going to be there." Anthropic, which will list under the symbol ANT on 19 November, will be the first fully AI-focused company to go public, making it a test case for the future of the technology. At $1.3tn, Anthropic's possible valuation is below SpaceX, Elon Musk's rocket, satellite and artificial intelligence company, which listed its shares in June and was valued at nearly $1.8tn. - Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe - Published4 days ago - Anthropic's blockbuster share listing - 5 surprising things we now know - Published26 October Anthropic is just five years old. It was co-founded in 2021 by brother and sister Dario and Daniela Amodei along with five others – all of whom worked at OpenAI, the rival AI giant behind ChatGPT. It announced its intention to list on the stock market in June and OpenAI followed suit. That listing is now expected to occur early next year. The listing announcements were followed by a series of incidents involving AI agents, which are bots designed to operate somewhat autonomously, going rogue. Current and former staff of both companies have warned AI technology was being developed without the ability to protect humanity from possible future harms enacted by AI. Anthropic has admitted that advanced AI systems "could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponised, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy". The company has reiterated promises to develop AI to be beneficial to people. It has warned investors its future success depends largely on its ability to develop the most advanced AI models, and that "any failure to do so could adversely affect our business".

items.articleText: Tüm hisseler devredildi: İki kamu bankası TVF çatısı altında buluştu - Türkiye Varlık Fonu, Ziraat Katılım ve Halk Katılım bankalarının tüm hisselerini TVF Katılım Finans Yatırımları AŞ'ye devretti. İşlemlerin tamamlanmasıyla iki kamu sermayeli katılım bankası aynı çatı altında toplandı. Türkiye Varlık Fonu (TVF), Ziraat Katılım ve Halk Katılım bankalarının paylarının tamamının TVF Katılım Finans Yatırımları AŞ'ye devredildiğini duyurdu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle TVF'nin internet sitesinden yapılan açıklamaya göre, 7 Ekim 2026 tarihinde duyurulan pay devir sözleşmeleri kapsamında ilgili yasal ve düzenleyici süreçler tamamlandı. Devir işlemlerinin kapanışı da gerçekleştirildi. Kamu sermayeli katılım bankaları tek çatı altında Devir işlemiyle kamu sermayeli katılım finans kurumlarının aynı çatı altında toplanmasına yönelik süreçte önemli bir aşama tamamlanmış oldu. Düzenlemeyle katılım finans kurumlarının kapasitesinin ve rekabet gücünün artırılması, finansal piyasalar içerisindeki paylarının büyütülmesi hedefleniyor. TVF'den katılım finans ekosistemi vurgusu Türkiye Varlık Fonu, yatırım stratejisi doğrultusunda finansal piyasaların derinleşmesine ve katılım finans ekosisteminin gelişmesine katkı sağlamaya yönelik çalışmalarını sürdüreceğini bildirdi.

items.title: Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December
items.summary: US inflation came in above forecasts in October, increasing expectations of a bigger rate hike in December and raising concerns for crypto investors.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December
items.summaryTr: US inflation came in above forecasts in October, increasing expectations of a bigger rate hike in December and raising concerns for crypto investors.
items.articleText: Hot US inflation raises odds of half-point Fed hike in December US inflation came in above forecasts in October, increasing expectations of a bigger rate hike in December and raising concerns for crypto investors. Crypto industry experts warned on Tuesday that higher-than-expected US inflation could lead to a another Federal Reserve interest rate hike, making borrowing more expensive and potentially discouraging investment in cryptocurrencies. The US Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% month over month in October, above economists’ forecast of 0.3%, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics - a slower increase than September’s 0.6% rise. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, rose 0.3%, above the expected 0.2%. Currently, the Federal Reserve holds its benchmark interest rate at 3.75% to 4.00%, after raising it by a quarter-point in September and leaving it unchanged in October. The report came just a few hours after Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said in London that another core inflation reading of 0.3% or higher could prompt the Fed to consider a larger interest rate hike in December. “In that case, I believe a 50-basis-point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting,” Waller said. “Hiking only 25-basis-points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take.” Markets were already pricing a quarter-point Fed hike in December. Tuesday’s data and Waller’s remarks are now raising the odds that the Fed would tighten monetary policy more aggressively in December, potentially raising borrowing costs and squeezing returns for leveraged crypto investors. Related: US midterm elections 2026 as it happened: Democrats win control of Congress Crypto experts warn of higher borrowing costs After the CPI release, traders were pricing in slightly more than a quarter point of Fed tightening for December, according to Jeff Anderson, head of US at crypto trading firm STS Digital. “Following today’s CPI release, markets are now pricing approximately 27 basis points of tightening into the December rate curve,” Anderson said in comments shared with Cointelegraph. “The prospect of another rate hike is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore.” CME FedWatch data as of 16:28 UTC on Tuesday showed an 88.3% chance of a quarter-point rate hike in December and an 11.7% chance of a half-point increase. Meanwhile, the broader crypto market was trading lower following the report, with total market capitalization falling 1.6% over the past 24 hours to $2.57 trillion, according to CoinGecko. Bitcoin (BTC) traded near $73,274, down 2% over the past 24 hours, while Ether (ETH) fell nearly 5% to around $2,028 and Solana (SOL) dropped 5.6% to $82. Experts said that higher interest rates could also reduce profits from some crypto investments. Adam Haeems, head of asset management at Tesseract Group, told Cointelegraph that investors who borrow money to make other investments could earn less if borrowing becomes more expensive. “Carry strategies earn the gap between what their assets yield and what they pay to borrow, so they are squeezed when borrowing costs rise relative to that yield,” Haeems said. “Over the past two weeks the rate paid to USDC lenders on Aave’s main market ranged from about 3.2% to 7%, while three-month Treasury yields stayed close to 4.2%.” The difference, in turn, could influence where investors put their money, especially if traditional investments offer better returns with less risk. Inflation adds to pressure after US midterms The inflation report also came a week after the US midterm elections, in which Democrats won control of both the House and Senate. “There is also likely to be growing political pressure from a blue Congress to bring inflation under control, potentially reinforcing the case for higher rates,” Anderson said. Still, he added that he remained skeptical about whether further rate hikes would address the underlying causes of inflation. While Congress does not set interest rates, lawmakers can influence economic policy and crypto regulation. For instance, the CLARITY Act, a bill aimed at creating clearer crypto rules for the US, has been stalled since January amid disagreements between Democrats and Republicans. The shift in congressional power combined with the possibility of higher borrowing costs could create even more uncertainty for crypto investors, experts said. Magazine: Wall Street killed Bitcoin’s wild rallies: 10x’s Markus Thielen

items.title: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
items.summary: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says
items.summaryTr: Delegations from Kyiv, Washington and Moscow are in the United Arab Emirates for the first trilateral talks since February.
items.articleText: First day of Ukraine peace talks constructive, Zelensky says - Published The first of two days of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine has concluded in Abu Dhabi. While senior officials from Kyiv and Moscow were tight-lipped after the four hour-long discussions, President Volodymyr Zelensky, who was not at the talks, said they had proved "constructive and quite substantive". Speaking from Paris, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said the meeting had been "very productive". Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said earlier that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario. Zelensky also said that humanitarian issues such as prisoner of war exchanges had been discussed. At the start of Tuesday's talks President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, told delegates that the US had "narrowed the gaps" between the two sides, without providing details, and hoped to move towards a "solution that hopefully ends the war". Kushner had said earlier the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine. He and Trump peace envoy Steve Witkoff also met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials on the sidelines of the main meeting. Until now European leaders have largely been excluded from peace talks, but they have pushed to be included in the discussions amid concerns that decisions about their continent's security would be made without them. The Americans appear to support this, with Rubio acknowledging during a visit to Paris that the Europeans "are a part of solving this problem for the long term". However, "the Russians have a bad taste in their mouth with the Europeans", according to a US official. Some proposals favoured by EU officials - such as calling an unconditional ceasefire as a prerequisite for peace negotiations - are routinely rejected by Moscow. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Tuesday that a truce would just allow Kyiv to regroup. "We will not agree to it," he said. Moscow and Kyiv's positions are still far apart on ending the conflict. A key area of disagreement involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia. Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are crucial to its future security. While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately". However, he acknowledged the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture". "They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other." For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it comes under attack again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from Eastern Europe – which would be alarming to Europeans. The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022. The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since. From the start of his second term in office, US President Donald Trump – who once boasted he could end the war in Ukraine within a day – has spearheaded several rounds of talks to end the conflict, albeit with little success. Meanwhile, his increasingly conciliatory approach towards Moscow has fuelled deep unease in Kyiv and across the European Union. After meeting Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington last week, Trump touted a forthcoming "big, beautiful agreement" on Ukraine that "might involve all of Europe". Many in Ukraine are sceptical that this would result in a fair peace. Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believed Trump wanted "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv. The only way to make Russia's Vladimir Putin start real negotiations was by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said. "While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war". Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi includes Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky. Kyiv has sent several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya. Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof that Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms. On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations". "This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism." Speaking from Paris, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said the meeting had been "very productive". Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said earlier that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario. Zelensky also said that humanitarian issues such as prisoner of war exchanges had been discussed. items.summaryTr: Yapı Kredi, uluslararası piyasalardan yaklaşık 933 milyon dolar tutarında sendikasyon kredisi sağladı. 18 ülkeden 40 finansal kurumun katıldığı anlaşma, 367 ve 734 gün vadeli dört ayrı dilimden oluştu.
items.articleText: Yapı Kredi'den (YKBNK) 933 milyon dolarlık dev sendikasyon kredisi! İşte detaylar - Yapı Kredi, uluslararası piyasalardan yaklaşık 933 milyon dolar tutarında sendikasyon kredisi sağladı. 18 ülkeden 40 finansal kurumun katıldığı anlaşma, 367 ve 734 gün vadeli dört ayrı dilimden oluştu. Yapı ve Kredi Bankası, yılın ikinci yarısında uluslararası piyasalardan yaklaşık 933 milyon dolar tutarında sendikasyon kredisi sağladı. Bankadan yapılan açıklamaya göre anlaşmaya 18 ülkeden 40 finansal kurum katıldı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 367 ve 734 gün vadeli dört ayrı dilimden oluşan kredinin ortak koordinatörlüğünü Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank, Bank of America, Emirates NBD ve Standard Chartered üstlendi. İşlemin aracılığını ise Emirates NBD gerçekleştirdi. Kredinin detayları belli oldu Sendikasyon kredisi kapsamında 367 gün vadeli 349 milyon dolar ve 356,5 milyon avro, 734 gün vadeli ise 97 milyon dolar ve 77 milyon avro finansman sağlandı. Kredinin maliyeti vade ve para birimine göre farklılık gösterdi. Buna göre 367 gün vadeli dilimlerde dolar için SOFR + yüzde 1,25, avro için Euribor + yüzde 1,00 maliyet belirlendi. 734 gün vadeli dilimlerde ise dolar maliyeti SOFR + yüzde 1,75, avro maliyeti Euribor + yüzde 1,45 oldu. Erün: Türkiye ekonomisine duyulan güvenin göstergesi Yapı Kredi Üst Yöneticisi (CEO) Gökhan Erün, uluslararası piyasalardan sağlanan kaynağın bankanın finansal yapısına ve Türkiye ekonomisine duyulan güveni gösterdiğini belirtti. Erün, yaklaşık 933 milyon dolarlık işlemin uluslararası finans kuruluşlarıyla kurulan uzun soluklu ilişkilerin bir yansıması olduğunu ifade etti. Uluslararası kuruluşların ilgisinin arkasında bankanın sağlam bilanço yapısı, etkin risk yönetimi ve sürdürülebilir büyüme anlayışının bulunduğunu vurgulayan Erün, gelecek dönemde kaynak çeşitliliğini artırmaya ve reel sektörün finansman ihtiyaçlarını desteklemeye devam edeceklerini kaydetti.

items.articleText: Borsa İstanbul’da 7 şirketten KAP açıklaması: Milyarlık anlaşmalar ve yeni yatırımlar Borsa İstanbul'da 7 şirketten yeni iş, yatırım ve finansman açıklaması geldi. Yapı Kredi 933 milyon dolarlık kredi sağlarken, Aksa Enerji Gabon'da kapasite artırdı. Kardemir Çelik GES kredisi aldı, Halkbank 14,8 milyar TL'lik devri tamamladı. YAPI KREDİ'DEN 933 MİLYON DOLARLIK SENDİKASYON KREDİSİ Yapı ve Kredi Bankası (YKBNK), 18 ülkeden 40 finansal kurumun katılımıyla yaklaşık 933 milyon dolar tutarında sendikasyon kredisi anlaşması imzaladı. Dört ayrı dilimden oluşan kredinin 367 gün vadeli kısmında 349 milyon dolar ve 356,5 milyon avro, 734 gün vadeli kısmında ise 97 milyon dolar ve 77 milyon avro finansman sağlandı. 367 gün vadeli dolar ve avro dilimlerinin maliyeti sırasıyla SOFR + yüzde 1,25 ve Euribor + yüzde 1 olurken, 734 gün vadeli dilimlerde maliyet SOFR + yüzde 1,75 ve Euribor + yüzde 1,45 olarak gerçekleşti. PEGASUS EKİMDE 4,21 MİLYON YOLCU TAŞIDI Pegasus Hava Taşımacılığı (PGSUS), Ekim 2026 trafik sonuçlarını açıkladı. Şirketin toplam yolcu sayısı geçen yılın aynı ayına göre yüzde 4 artarak 4,21 milyona yükseldi. İç hatlarda yolcu sayısı yüzde 14 artışla 1,55 milyona çıkarken, dış hatlarda yüzde 1 düşüşle 2,66 milyon oldu. Toplam doluluk oranı ise 0,5 puan gerileyerek yüzde 88,2 olarak gerçekleşti. Pegasus'un Ocak-Ekim dönemindeki toplam yolcu sayısı da yıllık yüzde 5 artışla 37,64 milyona ulaştı. AKSA ENERJİ'DEN GABON'DA 80 MW'LIK KAPASİTE ARTIŞI Aksa Enerji (AKSEN), Gabon Cumhuriyeti Elektrik Kurumu SEEG ile imzaladığı ek protokolle Libreville'deki elektrik santralinin kurulu gücünü 80 MW artırma kararı aldı. Daha önce 100 MW Libreville ve 45 MW Port Gentil olmak üzere toplam 145 MW kapasiteli santrallerin kurulması ve işletilmesi için anlaşma imzalayan şirket, yeni düzenlemeyle Libreville'deki toplam kapasiteyi 180 MW'a çıkaracak. Ek protokolle anlaşmanın süresi 10 yıldan 15 yıla uzatıldı. Mevcut 145 MW'lık santrallerin 2026 sonuna, ilave 80 MW'lık kapasitenin ise 2028 sonuna kadar devreye alınması planlanıyor. AYES ÇELİK'İN ALİAĞA FABRİKASINDA ÜRETİM BAŞLADI Ayes Çelik Hasır ve Çit Sanayi (AYES), yatırım sürecini tamamladığı Aliağa fabrikasında üretime başladığını duyurdu. Şirketin açıklamasına göre fabrikadaki kurulum, test ve devreye alma çalışmaları başarıyla tamamlandı. Böylece tesiste üretim faaliyetine geçildi. QUICK SİGORTA 10 AYLIK PRİM ÜRETİMİNİ AÇIKLADI Quick Sigorta (QUICK), 1 Ocak-31 Ekim 2026 dönemine ilişkin brüt yazılan prim üretimi bilgilerini Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda paylaştı. Şirketin açıklamasında ana sigorta branşları itibarıyla düzenlenen ve henüz denetimden geçmemiş prim üretimi verilerine yer verildi. Ancak paylaşılan metinde branş bazındaki prim tutarları bulunmuyor. KARDEMİR ÇELİK'TEN 14 MİLYON EUROLUK GES KREDİSİ Kardemir Çelik Sanayi (KARCL), Van ve Muş'ta gerçekleştireceği toplam 28,11 MWp kurulu gücündeki güneş enerjisi santrali yatırımları için 13 milyon 986 bin 926 avroluk kredi sözleşmesi imzaladı. DZ Bank AG Deutsche ile 5 Kasım 2026 tarihinde imzalanan sözleşme, Sinosure sigortası kapsamında gerçekleştirildi. Kredinin geri ödeme vadesi 9,5 yıl olarak belirlendi. Şirket, GES projelerinin sözleşme tarihinden itibaren yaklaşık 7 ay içinde tamamen devreye alınmasını bekliyor. Yatırımın enerji maliyetlerini düşürmesi ve kârlılığa katkı sağlaması hedefleniyor. HALKBANK, HALK KATILIM BANKASI'NI 14,8 MİLYAR TL'YE DEVRETTİ Halkbank (HALKB), sermayesinin yüzde 99,99'una sahip olduğu Halk Katılım Bankası'ndaki paylarının tamamını TVF Katılım Finans Yatırımları A.Ş.'ye devretti. Devir işlemleri 10 Kasım 2026 itibarıyla tamamlandı. İşlemin toplam tutarı 14 milyar 799 milyon 999 bin 995,72 TL olarak açıklanırken, satış sonucunda 39 milyon 923 bin 999,72 TL kâr oluştu. Devir sonrasında Halkbank'ın Halk Katılım Bankası'ndaki iştirak oranı ve oy hakkı sıfıra indi. İşlem için BDDK izni 22 Ekim 2026 tarihinde alınmıştı.

Devir işlemleri 10 Kasım 2026 itibarıyla tamamlandı. İşlemin toplam tutarı 14 milyar 799 milyon 999 bin 995,72 TL olarak açıklanırken, satış sonucunda 39 milyon 923 bin 999,72 TL kâr oluştu. Devir sonrasında Halkbank'ın Halk Katılım Bankası'ndaki iştirak oranı ve oy hakkı sıfıra indi. İşlem için BDDK izni 22 Ekim 2026 tarihinde alınmıştı.

items.articleText: Ziraat Bankası'nın 3.çeyrek net kârı 50,3 milyar TL'ye yükseldi: İşte bilanço detayları YAYIN TARİHİ, 10 Kasım 2026 20:07 PAYLAŞ - Ziraat Bankası, 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde 50,3 milyar TL net kâr açıkladı. Bankanın net faiz geliri yıllık bazda 85,5 milyar TL'den 123,4 milyar TL'ye, net ücret ve komisyon gelirleri ise 22,9 milyar TL'den 29,9 milyar TL'ye çıktı. Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Ziraat Bankası, 2026 yılının üçüncü çeyreğine ilişkin finansal sonuçlarını açıkladı. Bankanın net kârı, geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki 49,7 milyar TL seviyesinden 50,3 milyar TL'ye yükseldi. Net faiz geliri 123,4 milyar TL'ye çıktı CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Ziraat Bankası'nın üçüncü çeyrekte elde ettiği net faiz geliri, geçen yılın aynı dönemindeki 85,5 milyar TL'den 123,4 milyar TL'ye yükseldi. Bankanın net ücret ve komisyon gelirleri de yıllık bazda artış gösterdi. Geçen yılın aynı döneminde 22,9 milyar TL olan gelir, 2026'nın üçüncü çeyreğinde 29,9 milyar TL olarak gerçekleşti. Kredi hacmi 5,5 trilyon TL'ye ulaştı Ziraat Bankası'nın üçüncü çeyrek sonu itibarıyla toplam kredi hacmi 5,5 trilyon TL'ye yükseldi. Bankanın kredi büyüklüğü, 2025 yıl sonundaki 4,2 trilyon TL seviyesine kıyasla artış kaydetti.

items.summary: The contents of the calendar, including hair clips and keychains, have been widely criticised on social media.

items.titleTr: Kim Kardashian's Skims offers refunds for $148 advent calendar after backlash
items.summaryTr: The contents of the calendar, including hair clips and keychains, have been widely criticised on social media.
items.articleText: Kim Kardashian's Skims offers refunds for $148 advent calendar after backlash - Published Kim Kardashian's Skims is offering customers refunds for its $148 (£110) advent calendar which has been widely criticised on social media. The accessories advent calendar promised "twelve days of fun surprises" but has been mocked online for the quality of its contents, such as hair clips and keychains, with some comparing them to something you would find down the back of a sofa. A spokesperson for Skims has told a number of media outlets "for some, the calendar didn't meet expectations" and the company has "personally contacted every customer" to offer a full refund or credit to put towards other products". The BBC has contacted Skims for comment. The shapewear and clothing business was co-founded by Kardashian in 2019 and has made the reality TV star a billionaire, according to Forbes magazine. Skims was valued at $5bn in 2025 when it raised millions of dollars in new funding. One account on TikTok called spicychathouse compared the contents of the calendar to things "my cat collects from around my house". Another account said it looked like "a bunch of stuff that Kim Kardashian was emptying out of her bedside table". A number of accounts showed people cleaning out their own sofas and claiming they had accidentally created the Skims advent calendar. "It is really interesting to see this kind of backlash," said Kate Vlietstra, senior director of food and drink at market research analyst Mintel. "It is something we have been seeing a bit more in recent years, particularly with the trend for unboxing on social media," she said, "It means that, inevitably, if people are not feeling they're getting the value that they have hoped for from the advent calendar...they've purchased, then yes, there is going to be a backlash." Advent calendars remain popular, according to Helen Wing, head of innovation at market research company Ipsos though she said that "the buzz around them has reduced a little bit". She said according to Ipsos research, people are willing to pay a bit more for an advent calendar but the contents have to justify the price tag. Using a £285 advent calendar sold by Liberty as an example, Wing said the upmarket department story is "very open about the value of the contents". "They will say there is over £1,000 worth of content," she said. "If you've got that reassurance when you're making the purchase, particularly if it is for a gift, then it is important to have some faith that the contents are actually going to be worth the money that you're paying." items.title: Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government
items.summary: Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has first chance to build a new government and oust the prime minister.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government
items.summaryTr: Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rival, Gadi Eisenkot, has first chance to build a new government and oust the prime minister.
items.articleText: Israel's new parliament sworn in as leaders compete to form government - Published Israel's new parliament has been sworn in, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot seeks to oust caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The former army chief has been tasked with forming a government after receiving more recommendations from members of the Knesset than Netanyahu, although not all those backing him are willing to govern together. Eisenkot's bloc of four parties won 48 seats in October's election, while Netanyahu's bloc won 53, leaving both short of a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. He has 28 days to build a coalition, with a possible two-week extension. Almost half of the new MKs did not serve in the previous parliament, while Arab-led parties have a record number of seats. Shortly after they were sworn in, Netanyahu and Eisenkot warned parliament about the perils of supporting a government led by the other. "[And] to those who are thinking of establishing a government that includes supporters of terror and haters of Israel, or that will be dependent on them, I ask you, are you prepared to be dependent on those whose goal is the destruction of the Jewish state?" said Netanyahu, alluding to the prospect of an Eisenkot-led government reliant on support from Arab parties. He also appealed for the formation of a government of national unity as the only way to confront what he said was the threat of "a nuclear Iran". Eisenkot sharply criticised Netanyahu's comments. "I sat and listened to the outgoing prime minister's delusional, divisive, hate-filled and shameful speech, exploiting a state occasion," he said. "I am now even more convinced that he is unfit to remain in office for even one more minute." The outcome of the election, which was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu, means there is a period of uncertainty over who will form the next government. Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister until then - a process which could take from days to months. One of the most dramatic results was the performance of Israel's two Arab-led alliances - the United Arab List and the Joint List - which won an unprecedented 19 seats between them following a surge in turnout among Arab voters. The Arab parties could therefore hold the balance of power, although Netanyahu has ruled out governing with them and three of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc have opposed including them in a coalition. On Sunday, President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with trying to form a government. Speaking at the president's residence, the centrist Yashar party leader called for the formation of a "national emergency government" - an implicit appeal to parties to put ideological differences aside to remove Netanyahu from office. This, he said, would "require creative and unconventional political steps". Eisenkot said any party or MK prepared to accept four principles could join his proposed government. Those are recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state; accepting the values of the Declaration of Independence; backing mandatory military, national or civilian service for all, including communities currently exempt; and recognising Hamas as a terrorist organisation and committing to dismantling its military and governing capabilities. The four requirements, however, could present significant obstacles to Eisenkot's potential partners. The conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jewish men, who are exempt from military service if they are in full-time religious study, was a major election issue. The ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism (UTJ) and Shas parties, which won 13 seats in total, have fiercely objected to attempts to change the status quo - something that all parties in Eisenkot's bloc campaigned to do. Eisenkot's four principles are also contentious for the Arab parties. Both emphasise equal national and civic rights for Israel's Arab citizens, who form about 20% of the population; the vast majority of Israeli Arabs are not required to serve in the military; and neither has publicly recognised Hamas as a terrorist organisation. The Arab parties could, though, help Eisenkot form a minority government. The United Arab List, which won eight seats, has said it is willing to be part of an Eisenkot-led coalition, while the Joint List, which won 11 seats, has offered parliamentary support from the outside. If Eisenkot accepted such an arrangement, he would still have to persuade other parties in his bloc to agree. Avigdor Lieberman, whose Yisrael Beiteinu party won seven seats, has so far refused to join a minority government dependent on Arab MKs. In return for their support, the ultra-Orthodox parties would be likely to demand major concessions on military conscription, which might be unacceptable to most of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc. The United Arab List, which won eight seats, has said it is willing to be part of an Eisenkot-led coalition, while the Joint List, which won 11 seats, has offered parliamentary support from the outside. If Eisenkot accepted such an arrangement, he would still have to persuade other parties in his bloc to agree. Avigdor Lieberman, whose Yisrael Beiteinu party won seven seats, has so far refused to join a minority government dependent on Arab MKs. In return for their support, the ultra-Orthodox parties would be likely to demand major concessions on military conscription, which might be unacceptable to most of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc. items.titleTr: Inside devastated front-line city that Russia wants Ukraine to give up
items.summaryTr: The BBC gains rare access to a specialist drone unit defending the eastern city of Slovyansk from heavy Russian fire.
items.articleText: Inside devastated front-line city that Russia wants Ukraine to give up - Published The dangers in Slovyansk are clear from the start. "If I say run, you run," Tetiana tells us. She and her colleague Yasha are escorting us into a city now under constant bombardment from Russian drones, missiles and glide bombs. It is raining and cloudy as we enter the city, and our military escorts call this "good" weather, meaning it is bad for drones. But the threat is still there, and Yasha keeps his eyes peeled on the skies, while 21-year-old Tetiana scours her phone for the latest military intelligence on likely threats from the air. They are members of a drone unit who call themselves Peaky Blinders and their distinctive emblem is a flat cap of the type made popular by the cult BBC TV series, although theirs are camouflaged. Slovyansk is one of four cities that make up Ukraine's "fortress belt" - a system of heavily reinforced defence lines in the parts of eastern region of Donetsk still under its control. Russia wants Kyiv to give up the fortress cities and they are central to talks on a possible peace deal that have resumed after nine months between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi. Ukrainians worry that doing so would make it much easier for Russia to advance further west, including to the capital Kyiv. Once inside the city, we leave our vehicles hidden under the cover of trees and venture out on foot. Yasha carries a shotgun – a last resort to shoot down Russian drones. In halting English, Tetiana tells us walking is safer than travelling by car. Abandoned vehicles litter the streets – recently destroyed by remotely operated Russian first-person view drones. The anti-drone netting that covers the roads is no guarantee of safety. Tetiana shows us a video on her phone taken a few days earlier. You can hear several drones buzzing above her, and then the cacophony of small arms fire as Ukrainian forces try to shoot them down. Tetiana admits it can be scary but explains how she felt compelled to help her country, abandoning her dreams of becoming an opera singer. Slovyansk is now a husk of its former self. Very few buildings have been left unscathed, with many reduced to rubble. Tetiana shows us a school recently destroyed by Russian glide bombs. Across the road there is a gaping hole in an abandoned residential block. Broken glass litters the pavement. The few shops still functioning are boarded up – making it hard to distinguish what is still open. Most have closed. Tetiana says the Russians are doing everything they can to intimidate people and drive them out of the city. That, she says, "is their strategy – to make people leave in chaos, gathering up their last belongings and fleeing amid enormous fear and suffering. They want people to have nowhere left to live". It is a familiar pattern already seen in other Ukrainian towns and cities in the Donbas – like Pokrovsk and Bakhmut. These are now ghost towns reduced to rubble, but eventually falling into Russian hands. Russia has already taken nearly 90% of the Donbas – made up of the regions of Luhansk and Donetsk - but its advances this year have all but stalled in the face of strong Ukrainian resistance. The White House is sounding positive about the revived talks in Abu Dhabi, despite Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's refusal to cede the territory. October was the deadliest month for Russian troops since the start of its full-scale invasion – with more than 54,000 killed or injured, according to Ukraine's general staff. Despite this, Russian forces are still making life in the Fortress Belt cities almost impossible. Before the war, Slovyansk was a city of more than 200,000 people. Less than 10% of those remain and the population diminishes by the day. But amid the wail of near constant air raid warnings, there are still signs of people clinging on to life here. Iryna works in one of the city's last remaining coffee shops. Slovyansk is where she was born. "I'm forced to walk around crying," she tells me. "How can they do this?" Life, she says, has become incredibly difficult. She has already lost her house. But despite her tears, there is still defiance: "I won't leave Slovyansk. This is my home." Inga, 53, was also born and raised here and continues to work in the city despite the danger. "It's stressful. Honestly, I don't even know what to say," she says, but she is staying because of what she calls the "fear of the unknown". "I simply have nowhere to go, and I don't have the money to leave or support myself afterwards." Nor, she says, is there anywhere else in Ukraine she would consider truly safe. We first met the Omega National Guard Special Forces drone unit two years ago fighting in the Kharkiv region, in north-eastern Ukraine. Just four of the original team remain - the rest have moved to other units, or they have been wounded or killed. Among the dead was the brother of the man in charge of the unit, Oleksandr, who now describes his unit as his family. He jokes it is just like the Peaky Blinders TV show – "but without the crime and the drugs". Back at their base they share a meal every evening. Oleksandr reads out a prayer of thanks for surviving another day – he says it strengthens their spirits. The meal is accompanied by classical music played on a speaker. It helps drown out the noise of the explosions nearby. "I feel this is the most difficult situation we've ever faced," says Oleksandr, who underlines the importance of holding the line. "We must be here to inflict maximum damage on the enemy. We're fighting here because this is where the most intense phase of the war is taking place. Russia's claim that they will reach the borders of the Donbas, seize it, and then the war will end is absolutely false," he insists. The remaining fortress belt cities provide Ukraine with a strong defensive line and are a major obstacle to any Russian advance. The saturation of drones in the area is also now making it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance here. Peace talks may have resumed, but Oleksandr notes they have not led to anything so far. "I really want this war to end," he says, "but do I believe these negotiations will succeed? No, I don't really believe they will". The next morning we are not the only ones making an exit. A dozen civilians have arrived at an evacuation point in the centre to be escorted out. They hold all the belongings they can carry and are taken into a bunker for their safety. Outside there is another heavy blast of small arms fire, signalling more drones are nearby. Alina Shyrko, herself a resident of Slovyansk, is co-ordinating the move of civilians out of the city and says the situation has deteriorated rapidly over the past few months. Families with children have already been ordered to leave. "Everyone is thinking about leaving," she says, "I'm thinking about it too." Ukraine still holds Slovyansk but its lifeblood, its people, are ebbing away. Additional reporting by Rebecca Hartmann and Volodymyr Lozhko.

Ayrıca Elite versiyonunda ÖTV avantajı bulunuyor. ENYAQ VE ENYAQ COUPE'DE 1 MİLYON TL FAİZSİZ KREDİ Skoda'nın elektrikli otomobil modelleri Enyaq ve Enyaq Coupe için tüzel müşterilere 1 milyon TL'ye 6 ay vadeli yüzde 0 faizli kredi fırsatı sunuluyor.

items.title: Some pupils 'struggling just to get a hot meal'
items.summary: Students speak out as school dinner prices are set to increase for the second time in a year.

items.titleTr: Some pupils 'struggling just to get a hot meal'
items.summaryTr: Students speak out as school dinner prices are set to increase for the second time in a year.
items.articleText: Some pupils 'struggling just to get a hot meal' - Published The increasing price of school dinners in Northern Ireland has left some pupils "struggling just to get a hot meal," one teenage student has said. Robert-Frederic, 17, is among pupils at Belfast's Malone Integrated College who spoke out after it was announced prices are to rise for the second year in a row. Post-primary pupils will pay an extra 15% on their canteen choices from January, while set meals at pre-school, primary and special schools will rise by 30p. The Education Authority (EA) said the amount parents would have to pay was still well below the average cost of producing a school meal, estimated at over £5.20. Families recently had to set aside extra money for term-time meals after primary and special school dinners increased by 50p in January 2026. At that time, post-primary pupils were informed they would pay almost 20% more for the food they bought in school canteens. Robert-Frederic told BBC News NI that the previous increase had already made paying for lunches "more difficult for all students". "Back before the price rise in 2026, you could get water, a cookie and your hot meal and now with the price rise students are struggling just to get a hot meal," he said. "Instead of just going off numbers on a page, you should actually see how it affects people." 'Pressure on parents' More than half (55%) of pupils at Malone Integrated College are entitled to free school meals but many others are from low incomes households. "It's horrible seeing people around me not being able to afford school meals," said 17-year-old Naomi. "It also puts pressure on the parents," she added. "Without proper lunches it can affect people's learning and their mental health." For 16-year-old Paddy, the last price hike meant he had to change his canteen choices at Malone. "Some of my favourite foods such as like the school chicken - that went up," he said. "It was around £2.20 and now it's £2.60. "And as a student that felt like I should prioritise getting to school because I only get £5 a day and £2.50 of that has to go towards getting the bus." The school's headteacher, Áine Leslie, said the price rise will put further pressure on families who are already worried about the cost of living crisis. "I think the cumulative effect of this will be immense, particularly families who have multiple children, both at a primary school and a post-primary school, and trying to make ends meet, it's going to become incredibly difficult," she said. When the prices increased earlier this year, she remembers "sitting with the head of the cafeteria and heartbreakingly decide how much to put up each item". She said some students would be "worried about the stigma attached to this, and won't voice their concerns and won't ask for help" which was "really sad". Leslie added that not having a healthy, balanced diet or going without food will be a "barrier to learning". How much do school dinners cost in NI? The latest increase means the price of a paid for dinner in a primary school or special school, for instance, will have risen from £2.60 to £3.40 since the start of 2026. Pupils eligible for free school meals will not be affected. The rise in school dinner prices is not the only measure introduced by the EA in response to what they describe as "an exceptionally challenging financial position". There will also be a change to some menus in schools, replacing baked desserts with cheaper alternatives. Why are school dinner prices going up? Education Minister Paul Givan said he was disappointed and concerned but added it was due to underfunding of the education sector as a whole. "I don't want this to be introduced, but it is a result of the Education Authority not having sufficient funding," he told the BBC's Good Morning Ulster programme. He said education often bears "the greatest burden" during cost-saving exercises and argued his department should receive a greater share of Stormont's budget. Givan also said the "inadequate" funding that Stormont receives from Westminster was "bearing down on a huge number of public services in Northern Ireland". Stormont ministers are yet to agree a budget, despite weeks of talks with Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant, who has repeatedly said there is "no more money". At Omagh High School in County Tyrone, almost 30% of pupils have free school meals. For the families who have to pay, putting the price up could deter those children having "nutritious meals" according to its principal, Christos Gaitatzis. He told BBC News NI that the 15% hike was excessive. "What is the price index at the moment – is it 3,4, 5%? I would imagine that would be the reasonable increase that you would put on anything. "So they are going three times the value - to me it is unreasonable." He said the rise would have an "overall future impact on the health of the kids". 'Flabbergasted' Northern Ireland's Commissioner for Children and Young People, Chris Quinn, said he was ''flabbergasted" at the change. "School meals are not a luxury. For many children they are an essential part of the school day, and these increases will hit hardest those families already struggling with the cost of living." Quinn added it was "particularly difficult to accept" another price hike shortly after the EA advised staff and pupils to "wear more clothes" to cut school heating bills. "Children did not create the financial crisis in education and they should not be expected to pay the price for it," he added. What other costs are increasing? Payments which subsidise milk at about 500 schools are at risk, but the EA is to seek funding from the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs. The EA is also planning to offer more parents payments to transport their children to school rather than paying for taxis. At present, some parents receive payments if their children are eligible for free school transport but no private providers, like taxis, are available. Charges for EA music lessons for pupils are also set to rise again. 'These were difficult decisions' The EA said it was being asked to deliver services "with insufficient funding" at a time when costs, such as providing energy for schools, continued to rise. It said it hoped to save £20m by introducing the measures on top of £30m saved this year. "These were difficult decisions which sought to balance our commitment to children and young people alongside the requirement to live within the funding allocated for the year." - Published14 January - Published5 November 2025

Stormont ministers are yet to agree a budget, despite weeks of talks with Secretary of State Sir Chris Bryant, who has repeatedly said there is "no more money". At Omagh High School in County Tyrone, almost 30% of pupils have free school meals. For the families who have to pay, putting the price up could deter those children having "nutritious meals" according to its principal, Christos Gaitatzis. He told BBC News NI that the 15% hike was excessive. "What is the price index at the moment – is it 3,4, 5%? I would imagine that would be the reasonable increase that you would put on anything. "So they are going three times the value - to me it is unreasonable." He said the rise would have an "overall future impact on the health of the kids". 'Flabbergasted' Northern Ireland's Commissioner for Children and Young People, Chris Quinn, said he was ''flabbergasted" at the change. "School meals are not a luxury. For many children they are an essential part of the school day, and these increases will hit hardest those families already struggling with the cost of living." Quinn added it was "particularly difficult to accept" another price hike shortly after the EA advised staff and pupils to "wear more clothes" to cut school heating bills. "Children did not create the financial crisis in education and they should not be expected to pay the price for it," he added. What other costs are increasing? Payments which subsidise milk at about 500 schools are at risk, but the EA is to seek funding from the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs. The EA is also planning to offer more parents payments to transport their children to school rather than paying for taxis. At present, some parents receive payments if their children are eligible for free school transport but no private providers, like taxis, are available. Charges for EA music lessons for pupils are also set to rise again. 'These were difficult decisions' The EA said it was being asked to deliver services "with insufficient funding" at a time when costs, such as providing energy for schools, continued to rise. It said it hoped to save £20m by introducing the measures on top of £30m saved this year. "These were difficult decisions which sought to balance our commitment to children and young people alongside the requirement to live within the funding allocated for the year." - Published14 January - Published5 November 2025

items.articleText: Pegasus (PGSUS) KAP'a duyurdu: Yolcu trafiği 37,6 milyona dayandı! - Pegasus'un toplam yolcu sayısı Ekim 2026'da geçen yılın aynı ayına göre yüzde 4 artarak 4,21 milyon oldu. Ocak-ekim döneminde taşınan yolcu sayısı ise yüzde 5 yükselişle 37,64 milyona çıktı. Pegasus Hava Taşımacılığı (PGSUS), 2026 yılı Ekim ayına ilişkin trafik sonuçlarını ve karbon emisyonu istatistiklerini Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'nda (KAP) yayımladı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirketin açıkladığı verilere göre ekim ayında toplam yolcu sayısı yıllık bazda yüzde 4 artışla 4,21 milyona yükseldi. Aynı dönemde arz edilen koltuk sayısı yüzde 4 artarak 4,78 milyona, arz edilen koltuk kilometre (ASK) ise yüzde 2 yükselişle 7 milyar 588 milyona ulaştı. Buna karşın doluluk oranı geçen yılın aynı ayına göre 0,5 puan gerileyerek yüzde 88,2 oldu. İç hat yolcu sayısı yüzde 14 arttı Ekim ayında iç hatlarda taşınan yolcu sayısı yıllık yüzde 14 artışla 1,55 milyona çıktı. İç hatlarda arz edilen koltuk sayısı yüzde 11 artarak 1,66 milyona yükselirken, doluluk oranı 2,2 puan artışla yüzde 93,4'e ulaştı. Dış hatlarda ise yolcu sayısı yüzde 1 düşüşle 2,66 milyon oldu. Bu hatta doluluk oranı 2,1 puan gerileyerek yüzde 85,4 olarak gerçekleşti. 10 ayda 37,64 milyon yolcu taşındı Pegasus'un Ocak-Ekim 2026 dönemindeki toplam yolcu sayısı, geçen yılın aynı dönemine göre yüzde 5 artarak 37,64 milyona ulaştı. Bu dönemde arz edilen koltuk sayısı yüzde 6 artışla 43,67 milyona, ASK yüzde 4 yükselişle 67 milyar 991 milyona çıktı. Toplam doluluk oranı ise 1,3 puan düşerek yüzde 86,2 oldu. İç hatlarda 10 aylık yolcu sayısı yüzde 13 artışla 14,53 milyona yükselirken, dış hatlarda yolcu sayısı yüzde 0,3 civarında gerileyerek 23,11 milyon seviyesinde gerçekleşti. Karbon emisyonu göstergesi geriledi Pegasus'un karbon emisyonu istatistiklerinde de düşüş kaydedildi. Ekim 2026'da CO2 gram/RPK göstergesi 55,3 olarak gerçekleşirken, geçen yılın aynı ayında 55,9 seviyesindeydi. Ocak-Ekim döneminde ise söz konusu gösterge 56,8'e geriledi. Geçen yılın aynı döneminde bu değer 57,1 olarak kaydedilmişti.

items.summaryTr: Halkbank, sermayesinin yüzde 99,99'una sahip olduğu Halk Katılım Bankası'ndaki paylarının tamamını TVF Katılım Finans Yatırımları A.Ş.'ye devretti. 14,8 milyar TL'lik işlem sonucunda bankanın 39,9 milyon TL satış kârı oluştu.
items.articleText: Halkbank (HALKB), Halk Katılım Bankası'nı 14,8 milyar TL'ye TVF'ye devretti - Halkbank, sermayesinin yüzde 99,99'una sahip olduğu Halk Katılım Bankası'ndaki paylarının tamamını TVF Katılım Finans Yatırımları A.Ş.'ye devretti. 14,8 milyar TL'lik işlem sonucunda bankanın 39,9 milyon TL satış kârı oluştu. Türkiye Halk Bankası (HALKB), Halk Katılım Bankası A.Ş.'deki paylarının devrini tamamladığını Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) bildirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Banka tarafından yapılan açıklamaya göre, Halk Katılım Bankası'nın yüzde 99,99 oranındaki paylarının TVF Katılım Finans Yatırımları A.Ş.'ye devredilmesi için Bankacılık Düzenleme ve Denetleme Kurumu'ndan (BDDK) 22 Ekim 2026 tarihinde izin alındı. Pay devir işlemleri 10 Kasım 2026 itibarıyla tamamlandı. İşlem tutarı 14,8 milyar TL oldu Devir kapsamında nominal değeri 11 milyar 499 milyon 999 bin 996 TL olan paylar satıldı. İşlemin toplam tutarı 14 milyar 799 milyon 999 bin 995,72 TL olarak açıklandı. Pay başına satış fiyatı ise 1,2870 TL oldu. İşlem sonucunda Halkbank'ın 39 milyon 923 bin 999,72 TL satış kârı elde ettiği bildirildi. Halkbank'ın iştiraki kalmadı Devir sonrasında Halkbank'ın Halk Katılım Bankası'ndaki iştirak oranı ve oy hakkı sıfıra indi. Böylece banka, Halk Katılım Bankası'ndaki paylarının tamamını devretmiş oldu. KAP açıklamasında, satış işleminin Halkbank'ın faaliyetleri üzerinde herhangi bir etkisinin bulunmadığı belirtildi. Alıcı şirket aynı ana hissedara sahip Halk Katılım Bankası'nın sermayesi 11,5 milyar TL olarak açıklanırken, alıcı TVF Katılım Finans Yatırımları A.Ş.'nin Halkbank ile aynı ana hissedarlık yapısına sahip olduğu bildirildi. İşleme ilişkin sözleşme 7 Ekim 2026 tarihinde imzalandı. Satış bedelinin belirlenmesinde özkaynak yöntemi kullanılırken, ayrıca bir değerleme raporu hazırlanmadı.

items.articleText: İmzalar atıldı: Türkiye ile Suudi Arabistan'dan 5 bin megavatlık yeni enerji hamlesi - Türkiye ile Suudi Arabistan, yenilenebilir enerji yatırımlarını genişletmek amacıyla yeni bir mutabakat zaptı imzaladı. Anlaşma kapsamında 3 bin megavatlık ilave kapasite için rüzgar santralleri, enerji depolama ve iletim altyapısı projeleri geliştirilecek. Türkiye ile Suudi Arabistan arasında enerji alanındaki stratejik işbirliğini derinleştirecek yeni bir adım atıldı. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın Suudi Arabistan Enerji Bakanı Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud'u kabulünün ardından, iki ülke arasında Elektrik Projelerinde İşbirliğine İlişkin Mutabakat Zaptı imzalandı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Enerji ve Tabii Kaynaklar Bakanı Alparslan Bayraktar, imzaların Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan'ın huzurunda atıldığını duyurdu. 5 bin megavatlık yatırımın ilk aşaması başladı Bayraktar'ın açıklamasına göre, 3 Şubat'ta Riyad'da imzalanan ve 21 Ekim'de yürürlüğe giren hükümetler arası anlaşmayla, ACWA Power'ın Türkiye'de iki aşamada geliştireceği toplam 5 bin megavatlık yenilenebilir enerji projelerinin çerçevesi oluşturuldu. Yatırım programının ilk aşamasında Sivas ve Karaman'da toplam 2 bin megavatlık güneş enerjisi projeleri bulunuyor. Bayraktar, bu projelerde kaydedilen ilerlemeden memnuniyet duyduklarını belirtti. İkinci aşamada rüzgar ve enerji depolama yatırımları Antalya'da imzalanan yeni mutabakatla, ikinci aşamada hedeflenen 3 bin megavatlık ilave kapasiteye yönelik çalışmaların hızlandırılması amaçlanıyor. Bu kapsamda yüksek gerilim doğru akım (HVDC) iletim altyapısıyla desteklenen rüzgar enerjisi santrallerinin geliştirilmesi ve batarya enerji depolama sistemlerinin kurulması öngörülüyor. Şebeke altyapısı da güçlendirilecek Planlanan yatırımların yalnızca yenilenebilir enerji üretim kapasitesini artırmakla sınırlı kalmayacağı, Türkiye'nin elektrik şebekesinin güçlendirilmesine ve sistem esnekliğinin geliştirilmesine de katkı sağlaması hedefleniyor. Bayraktar, yatırımlarla Türkiye'nin enerji dönüşümüne ve yatırım ortamına duyulan güveni somut projelere dönüştürmeye devam edeceklerini ifade etti.

items.titleTr: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
items.summaryTr: The Ritz hotel in Paris, which is still owned by the Al Fayed family, is one of the properties searched by police.
items.articleText: Arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say - Published French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse. The Paris prosecutor's office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released. In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities. It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner. - Mohamed Al Fayed accused of multiple rapes by staff - Published19 September 2024 Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor's office said. It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into "allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape". The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed. The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family. The Villa Windsor in western Paris, another property involved in the search, was a holiday home for the Al Fayed family. It was previously the home of King Edward VIII, following his abdication, and his wife Wallis Simpson. The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims: "At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities. "In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators. "Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations. "The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office." A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation. Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024. One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence. Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers. A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed's brother, Salah Fayed, who died in 2010. Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations. Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate. In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims. "Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further." The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities. "We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said. "We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated." The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like. "Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over." The management of the Ritz Paris told AFP news agency that it "does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour" and that it was ready "to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities".
