items.summaryTr: Anadolu’nun kadın hafızasından beslenen, kara mizah ile gotik anlatıyı buluşturan “Hortlak Kızın Hikayesi”, 24 Ekim’de DasDas Açık Sahne’de yeni sezonunu açtı. Oyun, Kasım ayında ilk kez Beyoğlu’nda, istos Sahne Aznavur’da seyirciyle buluşmaya hazırlanıyor.
items.articleText: “Hortlak Kızın Hikayesi” Kasım'da Farklı Sahnelerde Seyirciyle Buluşuyor Türkiye ve İngiltere ortak yapımı “Hortlak Kızın Hikayesi”, 19 Haziran’da Londra’daki Collective Theatre’da gerçekleşen ön gösteriminin ve 25 Haziran’da DasDas’ta gerçekleşen Türkiye prömiyerinin ardından yeni sezonuna başladı. Yazar Derem Çıray’ın kaleme aldığı, yönetmenliğini Işık Kaya’nın üstlendiği oyun, Cazu karakterine hayat veren Iraz Akçam’ın tek kişilik performansıyla sahneye taşınıyor. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle On yedi yaşındaki Cazu’nun ölümünün ardından başlayan sıra dışı yolculuğunu konu alan oyun, kuşaklar boyunca susturulan, dışlanan ve “öteki” ilan edilen kadınların hikâyelerini fantastik ve gotik bir anlatı üzerinden ele alıyor. Ölüm sebebini bilmediği için öteki dünyaya kabul edilmeyen Cazu, bir hortlak olarak yaşayanların arasına geri döner. Ölümünün ardındaki gerçeği ararken, bir yandan da kendisine anlatılan hikâyelerin izini sürer ve kendi hikâyesini yeniden yazmaya başlar. “Hortlak Kızın Hikayesi”, bastırılmış kadın seslerini oyuna özgü bestelenen şarkıların desteğiyle de sahneye taşıyarak seyirciyi karanlık, şiirsel ve düşündürücü bir yolculuğa davet ediyor. Tek kişilik performansıyla oyunun merkezinde yer alan Iraz Akçam’a, farklı karakterleri seslendiren sanatçıların kayıtları eşlik ediyor. Deneysel anlatım dili, fiziksel performans öğeleri, müzik ve kara mizahın iç içe geçtiği yapım, kendine özgü sahne diliyle güncel tiyatronun disiplinlerarası yaklaşımını bir araya getiriyor. 60 dakika ve tek perde olan “Hortlak Kızın Hikayesi”, 13 Kasım’da yeniden DasDas’ta sahnelenecek ve 15 Kasım’da ise ilk kez Beyoğlu’nda, istos Sahne Aznavur’da seyirciyle buluşacak.

items.articleText: Bakan Gürlek'ten fon soruşturmaları çıkışı: "Hiç kimse hukukun üzerinde değil" - Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, fon soruşturmalarında çok sayıda şüphelinin tutuklandığını, mal varlıklarına tedbir uygulandığını ve banka hesaplarının bloke edildiğini açıkladı. - Gürlek, tasfiyesi tamamlanan fonlarda yatırımcılara ödemelerin yapıldığını, diğer fonlara ilişkin işlemlerin sürdüğünü bildirdi. Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada fon soruşturmaları kapsamında yürütülen çalışmalara ilişkin bilgi verdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Suç yapılanmalarının mali bağlantılarının ve para hareketlerinin titizlikle incelendiğini belirten Gürlek, soruşturmalar kapsamında çok sayıda şüphelinin tutuklandığını, mal varlıklarına tedbir konulduğunu ve banka hesaplarının bloke edildiğini ifade etti. Tasfiye edilen fonlarda ödemeler başladı Yatırımcıların haklarının korunmasına yönelik çalışmaların devam ettiğini vurgulayan Gürlek, tasfiyesi tamamlanan fonlarda hak sahiplerine ödemelerin yapıldığını açıkladı. Diğer fonlara ilişkin işlemlerin ise sürdüğünü bildirdi. Gönüllü iadelerin hukuki sorumluluğu ortadan kaldırmayacağını belirten Gürlek, iyi niyetli yatırımcıların haklarının korunması, mağduriyetlerin giderilmesi ve suçtan elde edilen kazançların ortaya çıkarılması için ilgili kurumlarla koordineli çalışıldığını kaydetti. "Hiç kimsenin ekonomik gücü hukukun üzerinde değildir" Soruşturmaların kararlılıkla sürdürüleceğini belirten Gürlek, sorumluların adalet önünde hesap vermesi için sürecin takipçisi olacaklarını vurguladı. Gürlek, açıklamasında, "Hiç kimsenin makamı, unvanı veya ekonomik gücü kendisine hukukun üzerinde bir konum sağlayamaz. Ucu nereye giderse gitsin, sorumluların adalet önünde hesap vermesi için sürecin takipçisi olacağız." ifadelerini kullandı. Fon soruşturmaları kapsamında suç yapılanmalarının mali bağlantılarını ve para hareketlerini titizlikle araştırıyoruz. Çok sayıda şüpheli tutuklanırken malvarlıklarına tedbir uygulanmış, banka hesaplarına bloke konulmuştur. Tasfiyesi tamamlanan fonlarda hak sahiplerine ödemeler yapılmış, diğer fonlara ilişkin çalışmalar sürdürülmektedir. Gönüllü iadelerin hukuki sorumluluğu ortadan kaldırmayacağını özellikle vurguluyoruz. İyi niyetli yatırımcılarımızın haklarını korumak, mağduriyetleri gidermek ve suçtan elde edilen kazançları ortaya çıkarmak için tüm ilgili kurumlarımızla koordinasyon içinde çalışıyoruz. Hiç kimsenin makamı, ünvanı veya ekonomik gücü kendisine hukukun üzerinde bir konum sağlayamaz. Ucu nereye giderse gitsin, sorumluların adalet önünde hesap vermesi için sürecin takipçisi olacağız. 📍 TBMM Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonu — Akın Gürlek (@abakingurlek) November 10, 2026

items.title: Poland’s lower house backs sanctions bill covering crypto freezes
items.summary: The bill is now before the Senate and would broaden the grounds for adding people and companies to Poland’s national sanctions list.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Poland’s lower house backs sanctions bill covering crypto freezes
items.summaryTr: The bill is now before the Senate and would broaden the grounds for adding people and companies to Poland’s national sanctions list.
items.articleText: Poland’s lower house backs sanctions bill covering crypto freezes The bill is now before the Senate and would broaden the grounds for adding people and companies to Poland’s national sanctions list. Poland’s lower house passed a bill that would broaden the country’s sanctions framework and explicitly include crypto assets among the funds authorities can freeze when imposing sanctions. The Sejm approved the government-backed Act on Restrictive Measures on Friday by 240 votes to 202, with one abstention, and forwarded it to the Senate on Monday, according to official parliamentary records. The bill explicitly includes crypto assets, as defined under the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA), among financial funds that authorities could freeze when imposing sanctions. Poland’s interior minister would oversee the national sanctions list, with sanctions-listing decisions taking effect the day after authorities publish a designation. Affected individuals and companies could challenge the decision in administrative court, but the bill allows enforcement before a court ruling. Poland already maintains a national sanctions list under a 2022 law aimed at countering support for Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. The bill would expand the grounds for imposing national sanctions to include certain foreign interference and information manipulation that pose a serious threat to national security. The Senate has 30 days to approve, amend or reject the legislation. If it takes no action, Poland’s Constitution treats the bill as approved in the form passed by the Sejm, allowing it to proceed to the president for consideration. Related: US Treasury cuts off MEXC over alleged $16B in illicit transactions

items.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, Coinbase and Kalshi have joined four other firms backing the CFTC in a lawsuit over whether US exchanges can list perpetual futures tied to individual stocks, cybersecurity firm CertiK urged exchanges to impose hard dollar limits on hot-wallet holdings following the $6.3 billion Binance hack, and blockchain analytics firm Elliptic reported that North Korean hackers used newly created memecoins to launder stolen funds. Coinbase, Kalshi join lawsuit backing CFTC over US stock perp futures Coinbase, Kalshi and four other companies asked a federal court Monday to accept a brief backing the United States Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) in a lawsuit over perpetual futures tied to individual US stocks. According to a proposed amicus brief shared Monday by Coinbase legal representative Molly Abraham, the group also includes Kraken parent Payward, trading companies DRW Holdings and Jump Trading, and crypto investment company Paradigm Operations. The companies argue that stock perpetual futures fall under existing US futures laws. The filing comes days after a federal judge found that the CFTC likely “exceeded its statutory authority” in allowing single-stock perpetuals to trade as security futures. The case could determine whether US exchanges can offer retail traders contracts that track individual stocks without expiring. On Nov. 3, the CFTC announced that single-stock perpetual futures, or stock perps, could begin trading on US-regulated exchanges for the first time. The Capital Markets Alliance Association (CMAA), a newly formed trade and advocacy group representing traditional financial market participants and whose members include Cboe and Citadel Securities, sued the CFTC last week, challenging the CFTC’s authority to allow the contracts to trade. Crypto exchanges need dollar caps on hot wallets, CertiK says Crypto exchanges should impose hard dollar limits on their hot-wallet holdings rather than relying solely on cold-storage ratios to measure security, according to cybersecurity firm CertiK. The recommendation came as several crypto exchanges recently disclosed how much they held in cold wallets, seeking to reassure customers after the record Binance hack that targeted its hot wallets. Crypto exchange Gate reported that 88.26% of its total assets were in cold storage, while Coinbase said it keeps more than 99% of customer assets offline. “Cold storage is a useful measure of online exposure, but it is not a standalone security score,” CertiK’s research team told Cointelegraph. CertiK said crypto exchanges should consider setting hot-wallet caps for each asset and blockchain according to the strictest of three limits: a percentage of customer liabilities, estimated withdrawal needs and an absolute loss ceiling based on the exchange’s financial resources and recovery capabilities. “Flexibility should support operating liquidity, while hard dollar ceilings and circuit breakers limit potential loss,” they said. North Korean hackers create memecoins to launder funds from Binance hack: Elliptic North Korean hackers created memecoins to launder cryptocurrency stolen in the $6.3 billion Binance hack, routing roughly $430,000 through six newly launched tokens on the NEAR blockchain, according to a report from blockchain analytics firm Elliptic. Between Nov. 5 and 7, the hackers created at least six tokens on NEAR and used liquidity pools on decentralized exchanges to move stolen funds between wallets, Elliptic said. The tokens attracted almost no outside trading and were abandoned shortly after launch. The hackers used one set of wallets to swap stolen NEAR tokens for the new memecoins, then used another set to sell those memecoins back into the pools for NEAR. The swaps let them move funds without direct wallet-to-wallet transfers, though the transactions remained traceable onchain. Elliptic said the same laundering technique was also used following the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in 2025, when North Korean-linked actors moved at least $24 million through a newly created token on the TRON blockchain.

items.summary: Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027.

items.titleTr: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss
items.summaryTr: Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027.
items.articleText: Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027. Wall Street’s embrace of Bitcoin has created the “best buying opportunity ever,” according to investor Mark Moss. Moss co-founded the Bitcoin Opportunity Fund, where he is an advisory partner. In 2025, UK-listed Satsuma Technology appointed him chief Bitcoin strategist. Moss tells Cointelegraph on the latest episode of Trade Secrets that he first bought Bitcoin in 2015 at about $300, during a recovery from a $1,000 to $200 plunge. “It was so risky,” Moss recalls of buying back then. In contrast, today, “you have consensus from the US government and Wall Street.” “But most people still think it’s a scam,” he says. That skepticism opens buying opportunities as Bitcoin starts to cross what Moss calls the “chasm” between early adopters and mainstream investors. Banks and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have made Bitcoin easier to buy and financial advisers could help persuade clients who have stayed away previously to consider investing. Related: Strategy shareholders approve daily dividends for four preferred stocks Moss calls bottom but Bitcoin keeps falling Bitcoin briefly climbed above $80,000 after the Democrats took control of the US Congress in the midterm elections, then gave back those gains as tech stocks sold off. By Friday, it fell to $74,762, its lowest level since August and remains in the doldrums at the time of writing. Despite the selloff, Moss points to the reaction to the $6.3 billion Binance hack as a sign that sellers were running out. “The price didn’t really drop,” he says. Bitcoin fell to $76,320 after the breach and slid to $74,762 on Friday, erasing its post-election gains. It fell further to about $73,500 late Sunday, its lowest level since August, after Nvidia’s board announced it would investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. Bitcoin found another bottom after reports of Nvidia CEO’s scandal. Source: CoinMarketCap Flows into US spot Bitcoin ETFs swung sharply during election week. The funds took in about $75 million on Wednesday, then shed $430 million on Thursday. History is on the side of hodlers however. Bitcoin gained an average of about 53% in the 12 months after previous US midterms, Moss says, using data going back to 2014. That leaves three completed election cycles in his sample. He says he expects Bitcoin to set a new all-time high in 2027. Moss backs Strategy but would keep his Bitcoin Moss thinks the Bitcoin treasury company to own is Strategy (MSTR), but believes that holding Bitcoin yourself is still superior. Strategy began buying Bitcoin in 2020 and turned those purchases into a core part of its business. It has used stock and debt sales to fund its purchases, giving investors a way to bet on Bitcoin through a publicly traded company. By Nov. 2, Strategy held 849,327 BTC, more than 4% of Bitcoin’s maximum supply. “I don’t think there’s another publicly traded company that will outperform Strategy over the next ten years,” Moss says. Strategy has the world’s largest corporate Bitcoin trove. Source: BitcoinTreasuries.Net Leverage can help a Bitcoin treasury company’s shares outperform the cryptocurrency it holds when its price rises. But even if Strategy outperforms, Moss wouldn’t trade his Bitcoin holdings for its shares. Related: 1inch lawyer sees agencies driving US crypto regulation as midterms unfold Before Moss bought his first Bitcoin, he made a living buying foreclosed properties, fixing them up and selling them. He moved into property development, then built and sold a medical equipment business. He says he put the proceeds into Southern California real estate. When the market crashed in 2008, he lost it all. “The reward of being right is not worth the risk of getting it wrong,” he says. Even with his outlook for Strategy, Moss says he’d keep his Bitcoin and use only a small share of his portfolio to pursue higher returns through treasury stocks. A journey of $1 million Bitcoin starts with small allocations In Moss’s model, Bitcoin could reach $1 million under certain circumstances, when it competes with stocks, bonds, gold and real estate for a considerable share of investors’ wealth. The model estimates how much those assets are worth, projects how that pool could grow as the global money supply expands and calculates a Bitcoin price based on the share it captures. Financial advisers could help bring in that money via one client’s portfolio at a time, encouraging them to shift a few percentage points out of stocks or bonds and into Bitcoin. The scenario depends on a critical mass of clients doing that, to the point where all those small allocations add up. The model also assumes Bitcoin stays secure and decentralized. Asked what could derail the scenario, Moss pointed to a failure that compromised either feature. Moss says $1 million is possible by 2030... though hodler’s might have to wait until 2032. Hodler’s Digest: Vitalik ‘pivots’ ETH to store of value, crypto suffers after US midterms

items.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
items.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
items.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

items.articleText: Release Number 9322-26 CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Division of Clearing and Risk today issued a no-action letter addressing whether derivatives clearing organizations may use trust companies to conduct daily settlements with clearing members. According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
items.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
items.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-
items.articleTextTr: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
items.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
items.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

items.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
items.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

items.title: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
items.verification: Birincil kaynak
items.titleTr: CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report
items.articleText: Release Number 9316-26 CFTC Announces Semiweekly Publication of the COT Report October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig announced the CFTC’s plan to increase the publication frequency of the Commitments of Traders Report (COT Report) from once to twice a week by the end of 2026. Data from Monday will be published on Wednesday, and data from Wednesday will be published on Friday. Both reports will be released at 3:30 p.m. ET on their respective publication days. Under the enhanced publication schedule, the reports’ latency will decrease from three days to two days. The change follows the Commission’s recent Request for Comment and reflects its commitment to providing market participants with more timely information about trading positions and activity in agricultural markets. The CFTC’s Division of Data is leading the effort to operationalize the expanded publication schedule through modernization and automation while maintaining accuracy. “COT Reports have been an important source of transparency for decades. Following feedback from the agricultural community, I’m pleased to announce the CFTC will be rolling out COT Reports twice a week to ensure this information stream is as useful as possible,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. -CFTC-
